A society hierarchic in war and communal in all else is unrepresentable today, and the repair is a small map from domain to mode rather than one enum | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures); `domains/species/src/lib.rs` |
| SOC-recruitment-mode | Recruitment mode is the missing generator of a group's demography and its politics: nothing anywhere says how you get *in*. [[SOC-9]] already supplies the per-pair edges and the asymmetry — trust instant to break, grudges sticky — so standing is the fold over them, computed rather than kept | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (reputation) |

So the world holds fifteen peoples and NO meta-ethnic frontier in its conflict record — the precondition [[MAP-9b]] and [[SOC-5]] both need is absent. The straight line is the fingerprint of no decay. | SOC-assimilation-rate | Coherence is a race between recruitment and assimilation. A group transmits its norms at one rate ([[CUL-18]]'s generational floor) and takes members at another ([[SOC-recruitment-mode]]); take them faster than you can socialise them and it dilutes into people sharing a label and nothing else. One inequality names conversion collapse, imperial overstretch and the guild ruined by mass admission. Group processes run at wildly different rates, and the mismatches are where the failures live | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-secret-commons | A shared secret is the most fragile commons there is. [[SOC-information-economy]] has the individual case — value as rivalrousness times scarcity, guarded and leaking — but a *group* secret is held collectively and any single member destroys it permanently by telling, which no fish stock can do. So it is [[SOC-commons-regime]]'s problem at its worst: monitoring is everything, sanctions must bite, and the group is pushed to raise [[SOC-exit-cost]], because a leaver carries the asset out intact | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-two-size-ceilings | Group size has two independent ceilings, and which one binds tells you what kind of group it is. The cognitive limit is [[SOC-size-threshold]]'s: past acquaintance, reputation stops working. The economic limit is Coase's: a group grows only while coordinating inside it is cheaper than transacting outside, so its boundary sits where those costs cross. A war-band meets the first, a trading house the second, and a group that has met neither is still growing for a reason worth naming | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-size-threshold | Cohesion mechanism is a function of size, and nothing here models the threshold. Reputation scales as the square of membership, so below roughly Dunbar's hundred and fifty a group can run on everyone knowing everyone; above it personal knowledge fails and cohesion must switch to markers, explicit rules and delegated enforcement. That gives [[SOC-11]] the *cause* it lacks — an institution is what a group grows when it outgrows acquaintance — and it makes growth a fork: formalise or fission | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-contact-structure | Group structure is also contact structure, so the lattice that governs feud governs plague. Dense within and sparse between is what a bounded group *means*, which makes it an epidemiological compartment — and `CauseOfEnd::Plague` currently arrives without reference to one. The trade-off is real and derivable: [[SOC-crosscutting]]'s ties suppress conflict by denying it a fault line and *accelerate* contagion across the same bridges. One structure, two consequences of opposite sign | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures); `domains/history/src/record.rs` |
| SOC-two-sided-membership | Membership is a two-sided relation and the sides can disagree — claimed by self, crossed with recognised by the group. Both yes is the full member; claimed but unrecognised is the passer and the convert never accepted; recognised but unclaimed is ascription you cannot renounce, which is the trap beneath [[CUL-interstitial-niche]]'s persecution; neither is the stranger. Two facts instead of one, and nearly every interesting case lives in the asymmetric cells | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-kin-terminology | Kin terminology is a per-culture partition over one universal graph, and only six systems are known — Hawaiian, Eskimo, Iroquois, Sudanese, Crow, Omaha — each merging different relatives under a single term. Descent is already an axis ([[SOC-1]], [[CUL-2]]); this is the *reading* of it, and it requires an ego, since no kin chart has a view from nowhere. One substrate, many lenses: [[RENDER-9]]'s doctrine arriving in anthropology with a closed enumeration to draw from | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-corporate-person | Can the group own, and can it owe? A corporate group persists as a holder of property and obligation across the turnover of its members; a friendship holds nothing, so it dissolves into individual claims at every death. That single bit decides whether an estate fragments each generation or accumulates — which makes it [[SOC-death-edge]]'s inheritance question asked one level up, and the seam where a group meets [[UNI-25]]'s balance sheet | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-exit-cost | Exit is the axis [[SOC-recruitment-mode]] missed, and crossing it with entry gives a grid whose every cell is named. Chosen entry with permitted exit is the voluntary association; chosen with forbidden is the vow, the covenant, the gang you cannot leave; imposed with permitted is conscription with discharge; imposed with forbidden is caste and hereditary bondage. Exit cost then decides behaviour: a group you can leave must *persuade* and invests in cohesion, one you cannot may simply *compel*. [[UNI-25]]'s flow versus stock, applied to members | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-commons-regime | A group is partly defined by what it holds in common, and no resource regime is modelled anywhere. Ostrom found durable commons share conditions that are structural rather than cultural — defined boundaries, rules fitted to local conditions, those bound by the rules making them, monitoring, graduated sanctions, cheap conflict resolution, nested tiers — so a group's *durability* derives from its own shape instead of being drawn. The failure mode derives equally, and the resources already ship: NPP, water, ore, land | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-solidarity-axis | Cohesion has a second axis orthogonal to authority, and Durkheim named it. *Mechanical* solidarity binds by similarity: everyone does much the same thing and the group coheres through likeness. *Organic* solidarity binds by interdependence: specialists need each other, so the division of labour is the glue. Neither is [[SOC-authority-per-domain]]'s centralisation — an egalitarian people can be strongly differentiated and a chiefdom undifferentiated — and it gives exit a second cost, functional rather than punitive | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-sclerosis | Nothing here fails from the inside. `CauseOfEnd` is `{Famine, Burned, Plague, Fled, Migrated}` — starvation, fire, disease, flight, orderly departure — so every occupation ends by weather, violence or displacement and none ever rots. Olson supplies the missing endogenous cause: a long peace *accumulates* distributional coalitions, each individually rational and each a drag, until a settlement can no longer reallocate anything. Decline as a function of undisturbed duration, which only a deep-time world can produce | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures); `domains/history/src/record.rs` |
| SOC-crosscutting | Whether memberships partition or overlap decides if conflict is bounded. Crosscutting ties leave no such line: if the guild spans the clans, no dispute can align them, which is Gluckman's result. Both are computable over [[SOC-9]], so escalation dynamics fall out of the membership lattice instead of needing a conflict model | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-declared-vs-derived | Declared membership and derived cohesion are different objects, and [[SOC-11]] assumes only the second. The interesting cases are the divergences — a guild whose members no longer interact, a clique with real cohesion and no name — and there is no divergence to find if only one of the two exists | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (group structures) |
| SOC-agency-locus | Where agency sits is orthogonal to how individuals group, and the nonhuman cases need it. | SOC-belief-sharing | Belief propagation makes the *group* the error-correcting unit — the social extension of [[UNI-1]]'s belief tier. A lost creature has its belief updated by a knowledgeable neighbour, so the band's confusion stays low by circulating information. **Shipped (law only):** co-located agents reconcile belief by reachability from the receiver's current position; a creature alone keeps its memory verbatim, so the live world is byte-identical. **But belief is a per-tick home-anchored fold, so a shared belief is transient** — the vision needs [[SOC-persistent-hearsay]] | shipped (law) | high | [The Tidings chronicle](../chronicle/the-tidings.md) |
| SOC-contact | **Contact between peoples — raiding is one cell of a much larger space.** When two peoples meet, anything can happen: pillage, rent-seeking/tribute, colonization, genocide, assimilation, proselytization, employment, alliance (forced or otherwise) — and mutually beneficial trade. **The generative kernel is the *rivalry of the prize*, not a menu of behaviours:** a perfectly rival immobile good (land, a valley, a mine) admits only one holder, so contact over it is necessarily *conquest* — taking is evicting; a rival but *mobile* good (herds, grain, metal) can be seized **or swapped**, so the same covetousness yields raiding or trade; a rival, *self-moving* good (people, labour) can be taken **or hired**, so it yields captives or employment; and a **non-rival** good (gods, language, technique) costs the source nothing to copy, so contact over it is necessarily *peaceful* — diffusion, proselytization, assimilation. Trade and war are therefore not opposite moral choices but what one covetousness does to goods of differing rivalry. The material sibling of [[SOC-information-economy]], which already derives the *informational* case from "rivalrousness × scarcity"; it also recovers The Tumult's ledger-#8 **asset-mobility** rule (mobile ⇒ rustle/extract, target survives; immobile ⇒ conquer/displace), designed and then lost between ledger and spec. **The outcome space is a lattice of two independent survivals** — the *persons* and the *peoplehood*: both survive ⇒ displacement, tribute, alliance, trade, employment; persons survive but peoplehood dies ⇒ assimilation, enslavement, proselytization, colonization; persons die but peoplehood survives ⇒ attrition; neither ⇒ genocide. The shipped bake already touches three of those four quadrants (displacement via `relocate`, attrition via `WAR_LOSS`, extinction below `VIABLE_MIN`) through *one* mechanism, conquest-displacement; the unbuilt quadrant is the culturally interesting one. **The slice boundary draws itself:** one-shot outcomes are already expressible as `CauseOfEnd`/`Founding` chains in the occupation record and are cheap, whereas every *standing relationship* (tribute/Danegeld, alliance, vassalage, colonial rule, employment) needs a persistent inter-community relation — whose natural substrate is [[SOC-9]]'s derived typed-edge social graph and whose governance sibling is [[DOM-16]]. **The stated price of that was wrong and *The Tithe* re-observed it: the ledger's `Fact` envelope is ALREADY a dated entity→entity edge, so the first standing relationship cost one registered predicate, not a save-format change and a new subsystem.** That is precisely the dominance-hierarchy + collapse-release slice [[SOC-criticality]] had already deferred, rediscovered from the opposite direction — decent evidence the original cut was in the right place. Program frame for the living-community sequels; predation ([[SOC-criticality]]) is one child of it. **The deferred quadrant now has a measured argument for promotion, not merely a structural one (*The Tumult*).** The conquest-displacement mechanism was built and its cascade-size distribution adjudicated: branching ratio σ ≈ 0.051 over 2974 conquests, deeply sub-critical, because one-shot conquest supplies dissipation and stores **nothing** between relaxations. The standing relationship this row names is exactly the accumulation term — tribute concentrates value into a structure that can later topple — so the criticality result ([[SOC-criticality]]) and this row's slice boundary now agree on which subsystem is next, arrived at from opposite directions and with numbers attached. | raw | med | [frontier §living-community](frontier.md#the-living-community--history-as-a-baked-derivable-biography) |
| SOC-criticality | Conflict as self-organized criticality — raids should *emerge*, never be floored. **Built three times, FALSIFIED twice — not a power law.** Build 1 (crowding sandpile over [[MAP-61]]) had drive, no dissipation; build 2 (predation, gated by [[SOC-inhibition]]) dissipation, no accumulation, σ ≈ 0.051; build 3 ([[SOC-tribute]]) supplied accumulation and **doubled σ to ≈ 0.11 without moving the shape** — 0.48 decades of support, nothing past 3 displacements in ~22k conquests. What is missing is not storage but **conduction**: depth and collapse-release stay non-goals, so failure has no medium. | shipped (slices 1–2 — falsified twice) | low (measured twice) | [The Tumult](../chronicle/the-tumult.md); [The Tithe](../chronicle/the-tithe.md); [frontier §living-community](frontier.md#the-living-community--history-as-a-baked-derivable-biography) |
| SOC-multi-axis | **Weakness is only absolute when there is one axis.** Shipped as *position*: a terrain-derived defensibility multiplier on the raid dominance test's holder side, uncorrelated with strength by construction. Measured against a frozen baseline and **falsified as built** — peoples-alive-at-bake-end did not rise (identical extinction set before and after) and the entity-size distribution stayed geometric — though the count metric was specified as two halves and only one was ever wired up, so the claim is untested in the 76.7% of worlds already sitting at the count's own ceiling | shipped | low (falsified as built; the untested half is deferred) | [The Contour chronicle](../chronicle/the-contour.md) |
| SOC-sigmoid | Annihilation ↔ coexistence ↔ domination on one **saturating** response: nearly every world sits in the middle, and both extremes are *reachable but rare* — a world without goblins, a world under one government. Replaces [[SOC-criticality]]'s third ask with a different *variable* (entity size — Gibrat/Kesten/Zipf) rather than a rephrasing of cascade size (BTW). Carries a build constraint: rare extremes need **asymptotes, not clamps**, and Hornvale's bounds are presently clamps | raw | low (unmeasured) | [decision 0096 §3](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0096-diversity-is-terminal-and-rubberbanding-is-multi-axis.md); [the Confidence Gradient](../open-questions.md) |

The discipline [[MAP-69]] states for the underworld — output that *resembles* the trope, never an authored trope. Depends on [[SOC-sigmoid]]: a clamped bound has no tail to name | raw | med | [The Contour chronicle](../chronicle/the-contour.md); [[SOC-sigmoid]] |
| SOC-frontier | **Marginal ground is one field doing two jobs** — too poor to be worth taking and cheap to hold, so it shelters the weak *and* drains the strong. Measured, pre-mechanism, as the rank correlation between a cell's weakest-point defensibility and its capacity: mean −0.020, 95% CI [−0.069, +0.029], centered on zero. **The frontier reading is withdrawn** — in Hornvale's terrain, defensible ground is not, in aggregate, poor ground | shipped | low (withdrawn) | [The Contour chronicle](../chronicle/the-contour.md) |
| SOC-casus-belli | **An occupation records *how* it ended but never *why* anyone did it.** `OccupationRecord` carries `cause` (`Famine`/`Burned`/`Plague`/`Fled`/`Migrated`) and `ended_by`, so "burned, at the bugbears' hand" is committed history — but no field carries a *motive*: retribution, a succession claim, a stolen relic. Grievance exists at agent scale and nothing lifts it to community scale, so a war has a perpetrator and no reason. Kin to [[SOC-contact]] and [[SOC-inhibition]], which name motive as the missing factor at another scale. History-domain work, not a rendering campaign's to carry. | raw | med | brainstorm 2026-07-27 (The Blocking) |
| SOC-dense-settlement | **At most one alive community may occupy a geosphere cell, so no two living settlements are closer than ~110 km** — `Bake::vacant_habitable` enforces it. **Never a design position:** an artifact of `node_index`'s type, written up as a rule a week after it shipped. What it forbids is *rival polities in sight of one another*; several *sites* per cell stay derivable ([[SOC-settlement-tiers]]). Relaxing it moves world identity — epoch, census re-baseline, study pins → invariants — but there is no design argument to win. **Nathan wants this soon-ish.** | ratified (0102) | high | [0102](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0102-one-per-cell-was-an-index-artifact.md); [The Keeping chronicle](../chronicle/the-keeping.md) |
| SOC-flagship-selection | **A people's "chief settlement" is an identity that gets re-selected, and any metric keyed on it measures the re-selection.** `flagship_of` resolves the **first surviving settlement fact** of a species — the *oldest surviving occupation*, not the largest — and a conquest closes the raider's own occupation record and reopens it at the seized cell. So a raiding people hands its flagship on in ~35 % of worlds where a non-raiding one does so in ~6 %, and the records it loses are systematically **inland** (an inland cell has good neighbours to covet; a high-capacity coastal cell has few). *The Tumult* inverted an earlier preregistered hypothesis (kobold flagships less coastal than goblin ones) and the investigation found no one had relocated: 100 % of the coastal movement lives in the subset where the flagship *cell changed*, where a biased subset at 0.549 coastal was deleted and its replacements landed at 0.688, back at the founding-pool base rate; where the cell was unchanged the rate is byte-identical before and after. Two durable consequences. (1) **An instrument caution:** because the bake places every people from one species-blind pool ([[SOC-inhibition]]'s niche-relative gate is exactly what is missing), the shipped model predicts a **zero** difference between peoples on any flagship-cell property — so such a test measures draw noise plus survivorship, never a niche claim; the falsified test was retired with a tombstone and replaced by one on the axis the bake does differentiate (disposition). Prefer a *provenance-classified* readout — which event class the flagship arrived by — over a bare property of "the flagship". (2) **A modelling direction:** oldest-surviving is a defensible seat rule but it is an accident of records order, not a claim. A *chosen* seat — the largest, the most defensible, the one holding the shrine — would make capital cities move for reasons, and is a natural companion to the standing-relationship subsystem of [[SOC-contact]]. | raw | med | [The Tumult](../chronicle/the-tumult.md) |
| SOC-information-economy | Information has value, so sharing is strategic, not naive gossip — the value of a piece of knowledge = the **rivalrousness × scarcity** of the resource it points to (the location of grass is worthless to hoard; a gold vein or the best fishing hole is a *guarded* secret, because sharing invites competition and depletion). So creatures share selectively: cheap/abundant-resource info freely, scarce-resource info guarded; freely with kin/reciprocators, withheld from rivals — wiring in [[SOC-9]]'s trust/allegiance graph and `SocietyVector.sociality`/`in_group_radius`. **Key connection — information LEAKS, it doesn't only flow:** you can be *seen* going to the fishing hole, so observation extracts a secret without consent — exactly [[MAP-perceive-apertures]]'s *"being seen is the dual of seeing."* Secrets therefore have **security** (can you reach your vein unobserved?), and stealth/exposure becomes economically meaningful. | SOC-tribute | **Extraction as a negotiation under mutual ignorance — the accumulation term [[SOC-criticality]] measured missing.** A raid whose prize is *mobile* (its people and product) **subordinates** rather than evicts, so a dominant grows without moving; the ledger already had the shape. Extraction is a discount-rate family on the patron's horizon. Deferred: protection, depth, collapse-release. | shipped | high (measured) | [The Tithe](../chronicle/the-tithe.md); [frontier §living-community](frontier.md#the-living-community--history-as-a-baked-derivable-biography) |

## The culture domain — enrichment directions

Twenty concrete enrichments of the *shipped* culture crate (`domains/culture`:
`subsistence` → an environment-and-psychology role ladder in `structure`),
generated by an ideonomy pass over its current shape. Each moves the crate
along one axis it presently pins — complexity (a flat role list), naturalness
(fully derived), homogeneity (one culture per settlement), source (environment
× psychology only), or connectivity (each settlement computed in isolation).
Several instantiate the elaborated social-structure (SOC-1) and memory-economy
(MEM) essays in the specific place the code stands today.

| ID     | Idea                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Status | Conf | Where                                                                                      |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| CUL-1  | Culture that contradicts its environment — `subsistence`/`structure` are today *exact functions* of biome × surplus × population × threat, so identical valleys grow identical peoples. A small drawn **founding disposition** (quantized, slowly decaying) biases structure away from the environmental optimum: path dependence and the maladaptive-but-persistent custom, the *accident* source the deterministic-derivation model forecloses | raw    | med  | [frontier §social](frontier.md#social-structure-as-orthogonal-axes--cashing-the-substrate) |
| CUL-2  | Descent as a first cultural output, orthogonal to rank — the shipped `structure()` is purely vertical (a role ladder); add **kinship/clan/moiety** as a horizontal axis so a settlement can be richly cultured yet flat. The concrete, shippable instantiation of SOC-1's elaborated-but-unbuilt descent axis                                                                                                              | raw    | high | [frontier §social](frontier.md#social-structure-as-orthogonal-axes--cashing-the-substrate) |
| CUL-3  | Roles as an obligation graph, not an ordered list — represent structure as *directed obligations* (labour/deference/tribute owed between rungs); the ladder becomes one readout of the graph, which also expresses reciprocity, patronage, and corvée a `Vec<String>` cannot. Raises culture's complexity axis from flat-list to network                                                                                    | raw    | med  | [frontier §social](frontier.md#social-structure-as-orthogonal-axes--cashing-the-substrate) |
| CUL-4  | The anti-institution / the levelling culture — negating "surplus grows a top rung": a psychology that *actively suppresses* hierarchy (levelling mechanisms, shame-the-chief) holds the ladder flat even under high surplus. Cheap (one gate flip on the `top`/`slave` rungs) and the structural sibling of EXP-11's ritual inversion                                                                                       | raw    | med  | [frontier §social](frontier.md#social-structure-as-orthogonal-axes--cashing-the-substrate) |
| CUL-5  | Culture that melts instead of freezing — the shipped structure is stamped `day: 0.0` and never revisited; wire the rungs and customs into the memory economy (MEM-1) so an unsupported caste **decays when surplus × will drops** (a shaman rung a famine cannot afford melts back to phenomenon). Turns culture from a snapshot into a maintained thing                                                                    | raw    | high | [frontier §memory](frontier.md#the-cultural-memory-economy--knowledge-as-a-maintained-thing) |

Gives diffusion (CUL-8) and MAP-9 contact an actual substrate to travel over, and is the connectivity-axis precondition for much of the rest                                                                                                          | raw    | high | [frontier §social](frontier.md#social-structure-as-orthogonal-axes--cashing-the-substrate) |

Nothing in code models one | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (norms and taboo) |
| CUL-norm-conditionality | Norms sort by *conditionality*, and [[PSY-audience-gated]] is the instrument that reads it. A convention solves a coordination problem and is self-enforcing: you keep to it unwatched because deviating costs you directly. A social norm needs both the belief that others comply and the belief that they expect it, so it holds only under observation. A moral rule is obeyed unobserved at a cost. Compliance measured with and without an audience therefore *classifies* a rule rather than requiring it to be labelled | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (norms and taboo) |
| CUL-taboo-two-sources | Taboo has two origins that behave differently. The anomaly taboo attaches to whatever straddles the culture's own categories — matter out of place — so it derives from a classification this world already generates, and cultures with similar ontologies should converge on similar ones. The marker taboo is *arbitrary on purpose*: costly and unmotivated is exactly what makes it an unfakeable membership signal ([[LANG-honesty-sources]]), so neighbours should diverge on those deliberately. Convergence against divergence is censusable | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (norms and taboo) |

[[PSY-suppression-layer]] and [[PSY-audience-gated]] together mean creatures show compliance they do not feel, so every observer estimates the norm from *displays* and estimates it too high — pluralistic ignorance, a norm outliving its own support. One public violation that goes unpunished then re-estimates it for every witness at once, and the cascade is deterministic. Emergent rather than authored, and it hands [[CUL-5]] a mechanism for melting | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (norms and taboo) |

The *energetic* allometric CAP-1 (basal-rate coupling in `allometry.rs`), Autotroph transpiration, and the ametabolic kinds' OWN drives (construct integrity, undead hunger, an elemental fed BY its element) remain deferred — the per-kind drive-authoring layer the gate opens | spec'd     | high                    | [BIO-2 design spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-bio2-life-history-allometry-design.md); [The Kindling chronicle](../chronicle/the-kindling.md); [the-kindling spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-20-the-kindling-design.md) |

## The biosphere — the living substrate

| ID     | Idea                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Status | Conf | Where                                                                  |

| BIO-6  | Flora & funga as fields — vegetation/fungal cover as typed functions over (space × climate) atop the biome prior; the terrestrial phenomena SEQ-4's observation path and the deep-dweller pantheon both want. **Reframed (2026-07-16):** flora is the *readout of **BIO-36**'s disturbance field*, not a climate classifier — shape it like the `language` domain (a proto-form plus a drawn cascade, present observable falling out, reconstructable backwards) rather than like `climate` (present conditions → label); the in-repo precedent for "observable = f(history)" is already shipped, in the wrong domain to notice. **Homogeneity resolves differently per scale:** a **composition vector** (60% maple / 30% beech / 10% spruce) at globe scale, individual stems *sampled from* it at room scale — the shipped MAP-28 → locale coarse-field inheritance is already exactly that joint. **Schema-adjacent, flagged not decided:** whether `Biome` stops being a stored primitive and becomes a **derived query** over the flora field (a biome as *discovered* readout of which flora each independently won, not an *invented* threshold a designer imposed) — UNI-20's derive-never-store cuts for it; `Biome` shipping in `scene/tiles/v1` as a cross-repo Orrery contract cuts against; an epoch/contract call, Nathan's. Note what the current model has no vocabulary for: **the displaced**. Nothing in `Biome` can record having been something else — the linguistic *substrate* cognate is the relict beech in the ravine the loggers could not reach, and `paleoclimate` already ships **refugia** as precisely that mechanism                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | raw    | med  | [frontier §biosphere](frontier.md#the-biosphere--the-living-substrate) |

A per-species trophic role (apex/predator vs. prey/producer) is the down-payment, confirmed absent from `SpeciesDef` today; v1 can derive apex-ness from body mass (BIO-23) alone, with an authored diet/trophic field as the higher-fidelity option           | elaborated | high (mechanics)   | [coexistence-stack spec §1.3](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-13-the-coexistence-stack-design.md) |

That makes scavengers viable where photosynthesis is not — the general form of an arid specialist starving in its own desert. Cost rides on [[BIO-6]]'s scale split: a coarse composition vector is cheap enough for the global bake, organisms stay lazy at room scale. The Delvers put three dwarves on this flat axis. | raw | high | brainstorm 2026-08-05 (Nathan); [The Tilth spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-04-the-tilth-design.md); [The Tense chronicle](../chronicle/the-tense.md); [The Delvers spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-07-the-delvers-design.md) |
| BIO-land-capital | **The land has no capital account, so it cannot be used up.** Capacity is a pure function of climate and terrain, so annual productivity is *income* and there is no *stock* — no soil depth, no organic matter, nothing extraction can draw down. Consequence: every eviction pressure in the bake is natural (ice, famine, war) and **not one is anthropogenic**; a place can never be ruined by its own occupants. Same shape as fisheries stock-vs-recruitment, the Ogallala aquifer, and income-vs-capital in finance. The Dust Bowl is unrepresentable. | raw | high | brainstorm 2026-08-05 (Nathan, from the Dust Bowl); [The Tense chronicle](../chronicle/the-tense.md) |
| BIO-reliability-not-mean | **Eviction tracks variance, not the mean.** Lieth gives mean annual NPP and the bake reads it as habitability, but a bad year evicts and the mean does not feed anyone in the bad year. Nothing in the model carries reliability, so marginal ground either supports a community forever or never — which is why removing the old hard zero flattened deep history from sixteen stacked steadings to one (The Tilth §5d/§5f). Churn should be a modelled process, not an artifact of a bug. | raw | high | brainstorm 2026-08-05 (Nathan); [The Tense chronicle](../chronicle/the-tense.md) |
| BIO-subsistence-feeds-capacity | **Subsistence mode is committed and never consulted.** `subsistence` (farming / herding / foraging) and `occ-tech` are both committed facts, and neither appears anywhere in `demography` or the bake — so the same productivity supports the same population regardless of how a people extracts from it. The Dust Bowl's lesson in one clause: the plains had adequate productivity for grazing and inadequate resilience for ploughing. Carrying capacity is productivity × mode, and the mode term is missing. The Delvers: no axis for ore, so "dwarves mine" was mis-authored as diet. | raw | high | brainstorm 2026-08-05 (Nathan); [The Tense chronicle](../chronicle/the-tense.md); [The Delvers spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-07-the-delvers-design.md) |
| BIO-niche-discriminates-weakly | **Two authored peoples can be ecological synonyms and the model will not say so.** `generalist_distinctness` proves human is not goblin-recentred via the gap between their fit dispersions. Under The Tense that gap fell 0.0472 → 0.0141. The discriminator survived — real-vs-mutated separation sharpened 4.00× → 4.55× — but the absolute distance between two peoples the roster calls distinct is small and shrinking, and nothing watches it. Wants a pairwise niche-distance readout over the roster. | BIO-40 | **Sovereignty should decay with distance, and the diversity it props up needs recalibrating** — `sovereignty_floor(mass, potency)` ∈ [0, 0.95] is added as an UNCONDITIONAL lower bound to every buffer-able condition response, so a goblin keeps **33.5%** of full habitat response at any temperature, moisture or insolation whatsoever and a red dragon **78.5%**. The name says *sovereignty* (imposing your conditions on a place); the mechanism implements **ubiquity** (presence everywhere at reduced strength), and its own doc calls that a virtue — "a soft preference that never excludes". The replacement was BUILT AND MEASURED in The Waterline and is preserved at commit `4f852fd2`: `value = devotion·exp(−z²/2)` with `z = (field − optimum)(1 − s)/width`, i.e. `effective_width = width/(1 − s)`, where `s` is the fraction of the environmental gap a creature closes for itself. Accommodation (a dragon warms its lair, shifting its effective optimum) and endurance (a wider tolerance band) are the SAME algebra, so the model need not choose; it needs no new tuning constant (the existing 0.95 ceiling becomes width × 20), drops `floor` from `eval`, keeps the buffered-vs-hard axis split for free (elevation passes `s = 0`), reproduces today's formula exactly at `s = 0`, and — unlike a floor — DECAYS. **Why it is deferred, and the finding that makes it a campaign rather than a patch: the coexistence diversity this project calibrated β to produce is substantially an ARTIFACT OF THE FLOOR.** With it, a badly-suited species holds K ≈ floor × conditions everywhere — comparable to the well-adapted one — and takes a real share; without it, K ≈ 1e-8 and the cell goes to a single winner. Measured: mean per-claimed-cell diversity **1.333** across five seeds (1.257–1.438) against the preregistered band **[1.5, 3.0]**, every seed failing. β = 2.0 was frozen by a 13-seed × 10-β sweep under the OLD response shape, so it no longer means what it was chosen to mean: the fix requires a re-sweep and a re-freeze. Also surfaced: `session_snapshot`'s golden bytes moved while world JSON stayed byte-identical — gameplay state depends on K where world state does not, a save-format-adjacent surface nobody has mapped. **REPOINTED by The Muster (2026-08-12): the diversity debt is NOT the affinity level, measured, so do not spend this row's campaign there.** Diversity swings **0.039 (2.7%)** across the ENTIRE per-kind λ range on both sweep arms and both rosters, and never approaches a band edge at any λ. Two further facts the guard's repair exposed. (a) **The commit-gate guard was structurally blind** — it built its component set with zero `biome_affinity` AND zero `habitat_realm` rows, both sparse stores read through a default on absence, so an empty store silently supplied the null hypothesis; both are now live and the assertion names the roster it counts. (b) **The band is ONE-SIDED and can only fail from below**: the derived ceiling is `0.75 × 18 = 13.5` while the mean claimed cell holds **6.4351** of the eighteen kinds (177 336 claimed cells, five seeds), so no mutation of the affinity store can reach the upper edge. ## The cultural-memory economy

Knowledge as a thing that must be *maintained*, and decays when it isn't —
the missing inverse of MAP-8. Cut by transmission channel so it stays
tractable; the spine is checkable, the generalisation is deliberately
deferred.

| ID    | Idea                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Status     | Conf             | Where                                                                                                 |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| MEM-1 | The memory economy — every retained fact carries an upkeep cost; held only while surplus × will exceeds it, else it melts fact → phenomenon → myth (the inverse of MAP-8); institutional death is a *symptom* of regress, not its cause (Bagnall); survival curves are a Lab metric                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | elaborated | med (spine)      | [frontier §cultural-memory](frontier.md#the-cultural-memory-economy--knowledge-as-a-maintained-thing) |
| MEM-2 | The floating gap — living communicative memory reaches ~3 generations, then a memory is institutionalised into cultural memory or lost (Assmann); the precise Alexandria moment, an era-tick event gating what historiography can recover                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | raw        | med              | [frontier §cultural-memory](frontier.md#the-cultural-memory-economy--knowledge-as-a-maintained-thing) |
| MEM-3 | Cultural stickiness — emotionally salient, minimally-counterintuitive content decays slower independent of institutional support (Sperber/Boyer/Morin); a per-item modulator making MEM-1's melt selective, and item 4's principled noise model                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | raw        | med              | [frontier §cultural-memory](frontier.md#the-cultural-memory-economy--knowledge-as-a-maintained-thing) |
| MEM-4 | Preservation as craft — a conservator institution spends surplus specifically to *lower* the decay rate of chosen items; the active-voice complement to MEM-1's rot, and the memory-side reading of MAP-3's liturgical damping field (diglossia, dead languages)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | raw        | med              | [frontier §cultural-memory](frontier.md#the-cultural-memory-economy--knowledge-as-a-maintained-thing) |
| MEM-5 | Institutions at large — an institution as a durable commitment of surplus to a function (memory/legitimacy/exchange/skill), each with a MAP-7-style founding→neglect→death lifecycle; memory is one cargo among many. The deliberate deferral: captured so it is not lost, scoped out of MEM-1 as the guard against generalising into worthlessness                                                                                                                                                                                                              | raw        | low (generalise) | [frontier §cultural-memory](frontier.md#the-cultural-memory-economy--knowledge-as-a-maintained-thing) |
| MEM-6 | Memory-cost inversion — a species that is itself a durable memory store, or whose memory-upkeep cost is ~zero (immortal perfect recall: the aboleth), inverting MEM-1's central equation; an outlier that halts the melt fact → phenomenon → myth for what it holds and stands as an archive others cannot afford — the un-forgetting complement to MEM-4's conservator                                                                                                                                                                                          | raw        | med              | [frontier §cultural-memory](frontier.md#the-cultural-memory-economy--knowledge-as-a-maintained-thing) |
| MEM-7 | Generation-length scales the memory economy — MEM-2's floating gap is pinned at a *human* ~3 generations / ~80 years, but that horizon is lifespan-relative: a long-lived species (elves) whose eyewitnesses outlive the institutionalisation window may never hand living memory off to cultural memory (the Alexandria moment never arrives), a short-lived one melts everything to myth within a lifetime. The whole MEM cluster's decay constants should be keyed to BIO-2 lifespan, not constant — EXP-5 wired this coupling into drama but not into memory | raw        | med              | [frontier §cultural-memory](frontier.md#the-cultural-memory-economy--knowledge-as-a-maintained-thing) |
| MEM-8 | **The artifact channel — MEM's missing fourth transmission channel.** Inscribed rots (the unpaid scribe), incorporated dies with the last practitioner, oral drifts into myth; a **magic item / cognitive artifact** carries the knowledge in the *object*, and its failure mode is unlike all three: **the knowledge does not decay — the capacity to make more does.** The instance survives; the recipe never does. So **"they don't make them like they used to" is derived, not authored** — ruins full of working relics nobody can replicate, with MAP-30's palimpsest supplying the ground they lie in. It also cashes UNI-1's one unpaid claim, roguelike identification: a magic item is a *cached derivation bound to an object*, so **possessing is not knowing**, and that gap **is** identification (an unidentified potion is a production you can trigger but cannot read; identifying it is inferring the derivation from the effects). Gives **three roads back to a lost lemma**, each with distinct economics and failure mode: *rediscovery* (experiment, UNI-1 inference; fails when phenomena are ambiguous), *comparative reconstruction* (LANG-5's shipped Neogrammarian cascade pointed at rites; fails when only one daughter tradition survives), *artifact reverse-engineering* (fails because the relic teaches nothing). Literature-checked off Frazer entirely: Hutchins's distributed cognition, Norman's cognitive artifacts. Distinct from MEM-6 (a *species* as the store) — here the store is an inert object | raw | med | ideonomy session 2026-07-16; [frontier §magic](frontier.md#magic-as-a-graph-grammar--the-debt-economy) |
| MEM-9 | **Suppression as craft — MEM-4 negated.** MEM-4 is an institution spending surplus *specifically to lower* the decay rate of chosen items; invert the sign and you get an institution spending surplus *specifically to raise* it — book-burning, guild secrecy, enforced illiteracy, the Sorcerer-King's templars, the index of prohibited works. Same survival-curve verification as MEM-1/MEM-4, opposite direction, and the same Lab readout measures both. Sharpens the memory economy from a story about *neglect* into one that also has an **antagonist**: Bagnall's inversion says the library was let go, but some libraries are *pushed*, and the two are distinguishable in a survival curve (uniform melt vs a selective cliff on one topic). Pairs with UNI-25's taxation posture — an issuer who monopolises a capability has a positive interest in its non-transmission, so suppression is not villainy but **portfolio protection**. What a culture pays to *destroy* is as much a portrait of what it fears as MEM-4's spending is of what it holds sacred | raw | med | ideonomy session 2026-07-16 |
| MEM-10 | **The abandoned project — MEM-1 pointed forward.** The memory economy is time's backward face; run its own equation the other way and **a plan is a fact about the future, and it has upkeep too**: a work is held only while surplus × will exceeds the cost of continuing it, and when the product falls the plan is not dramatically cancelled but *silently released*. **The unfinished cathedral is the forward face of the abandoned library**, and Bagnall's inversion transfers verbatim — *the fact that the cathedral was never finished shows the decline had already begun*. Yields a distinction MAP-30's palimpsest does not yet carry and which is legible in the ground: a **ruin of abandonment** (finished, used, then let go — evidence of a completed past) versus a **ruin of incompletion** (never finished — evidence of a *released future*), which say opposite things about the era that made them; the latter is also an anti-phenomenon in the strict sense, a meaningful absence. The rest of the cluster reflects too: MEM-2's floating gap → a **planning gap** (a work must institutionalise within ~3 generations or die), MEM-3's stickiness → **millenarianism** (minimally-counterintuitive futures outlive sensible five-year plans, same asymmetry pointed forward), MEM-4 → the chapter or dynasty that spends to keep a *future* alive. UNI-9's lich is the limiting case: the one agent who solves this problem by refusing to die | raw | med | ideonomy session 2026-07-16 |
| MEM-spread-and-uniformity | **Spread and uniformity are independent, and neither is a distance.** [[MAP-4]] and [[LANG-8]] score *reconstruction* against a true tree; this is the ground-truth pair underneath. A myth told everywhere but differently in every valley is a different historical object from one held rigid in three villages — and uniformity is the alignment reading nothing in the Lab takes ([[UNI-nonscalar-fields]]). If each copy carries its own depth-from-source, both read off *one* witness with no traversal, which is what [[UNI-34]] tracing and [[UNI-27]] meets need | raw | med | Phacelle ideonomy 2026-07-30 |
| MEM-founder-salience | Which founder a people remembers is a *selection rule*, and magnitude is the crudest candidate. The Particular ranks by peak population: measured and cheap. Each alternative is a different claim about transmission: **telescoping** (apical ancestor plus the recent, middle absent — genealogies hold constant depth, not constant span); **lineage-durability** (remembered because what you founded outlived you; `occ-founded-from` already chains it); **event-salience** (died in the flight, not founded the largest hamlet). Measured corr(peak, founded) = -0.33, so the rules pick different casts. | raw | med | brainstorm 2026-08-01 (The Particular, D2); the static half of [[MEM-1]]'s upkeep economy |
| MEM-founder-handle-epoch | **Shipped as a WIDENING, and the obvious narrowing was measured and refuted.** The old key collided by construction on 2/1000 worlds; the founding-side-only key it was to be replaced by collides on 732/1000 (1582 founders lost), because a raided founding and its same-year successor share every founding-side field and no depth of ancestry separates them. Shipped: the identity key (people, site, founded + one ancestry hop) with `ended` and `peak` folded on top — 0/1000 colliding, 0 dropped; the residual over 0-2999 is exactly {2634, 2898}, twin parents. Renamed every founder in every world. | shipped | high | [The Ell](../chronicle/the-ell.md); [decision 0127](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0127-identity-keys-and-discrimination-keys-are-different-kinds.md); sibling of [[MEM-founder-salience]] |
| MEM-founder-key-trim | **Refuted by measurement: no founding-side discriminator exists.** Same-site same-year twin foundings share every founding-side field at every ancestry depth; The Granary's day-grain stamps fail too — same-phase twinning makes the finer timestamp identical. Tail-less sweep 0–2999 post-Granary: **2261 colliding worlds, 5039 founders lost** vs 3 with the tail. The tail stays knowingly: recomputing its fields still forces a rename epoch | refuted (The Granary) | high | [The Granary](../chronicle/the-granary.md); `domains/history/src/flesh.rs::founder_handle`; sweep harness in `windows/worldgen/tests/suite/founder_collision.rs` |
| MEM-history-interannual-memory | **Layer 2 of fine-resolution history — weather that remembers.** The Granary shipped within-year seasonality and found raids cluster on OPPORTUNITY (aligned curves, full targets), not hunger. The Viking-age mechanism needs inter-annual variation: weather draws make some years bad; carry-over stores integrate them; bad-year runs produce cross-year raid flurries. Layer 3 beyond: full event-level resolution | raw | med | [The Granary](../chronicle/the-granary.md); [the-granary spec §2](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-23-the-granary-design.md) |

## Alchemy — matter, and the doctrines about it

| ID     | Idea | Status | Conf | Where |
| ------ | ---- | ------ | ---- | ----- |
| ALCH-1 | **The Crucible — a material ground truth plus the mostly-wrong doctrines inferred over it.** A program, not a campaign: a substance/production layer the sim adjudicates, and practitioners who induce doctrines about it and are *materially wrong*. Carved into The Reagent (ground truth), The Signature (the agent fold, and the thesis), The School (culture-scale transmission), with a UNI-2-gated violation tier named but unscheduled. The fourth site of [[UNI-1]]'s one-mechanic thesis, after The Surmise, [[LANG-5]]'s comparative reconstruction, and the [[MEM-8]] cluster \| **Campaign 1, The Reagent, shipped**: the eight latent quality axes, the five manifest signs, the seven-production grammar with mass balance as its admissibility predicate, and the composition-root carry from terrain vocabulary — the domain drawing nothing, so no save-format contract. Later rungs: The Signature (the agent fold, and the thesis), The School (culture-scale transmission), and a UNI-2-gated violation tier named but unscheduled | shipped | high (structure) | [The Crucible metaplan](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-the-crucible-metaplan-design.md); [The Reagent spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-the-reagent-design.md); [The Reagent chronicle](../chronicle/the-reagent.md) |
| ALCH-2 | **The provenance confound — the error term is derived, never authored.** Strip alchemy's vocabulary and it is *induction from a spatially biased sample of a function whose true arguments are partly imperceptible*. So: a recipe works in one valley and fails in the next because the reagent's hidden property differs, and the doctrine names the wrong cause. **The world is heterogeneous; the alchemist is local — that is the entire error term.** Lithology, ore grade, and `ConditionNiche` already vary by place, so no falsehood is ever written down; author what is true and locality generates the error. The same move [frontier §magic](frontier.md#magic-as-a-graph-grammar--the-debt-economy) makes when it reads the violation catalog off the property batteries rather than off imagination — and, like it, the content grows with the sim's fidelity instead of an author's word count. **Shipped half, measured at close:** the confound reaches APPEARANCE but not BEHAVIOUR — ore grade moves causticity and causticity moves only `hue`, so poor ore looks different and behaves identically (no production requires causticity; sweeping every commodity across the full grade range leaves the admitted-production set invariant). That is a real doctrine-of-signatures error, but not the recipe-fails-in-the-next-valley claim above. Coupling grade to behaviour via a causticity-gated production is The Signature's first task (owner decision at G6) | shipped | high | [The Crucible metaplan](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-the-crucible-metaplan-design.md) |
| ALCH-3 | **Substances are quality bundles, not a catalogue.** A material is a bundle of authored qualities exactly as a phoneme is a feature bundle; an atomic substance list is a lookup table, i.e. the catalogue-not-a-language failure [[CLIENT-language-not-catalogue]] and The Hearth's pattern discipline both exist to prevent. This is why `phonology.rs` is the literal template — one authored inventory, a derived per-world selection, an admissibility predicate — and its third re-instantiation after the phoneme inventory and The Hearth's spatial patterns. Shipped in The Reagent as an eight-axis `QualityVector`, with `fixity` and `volatility` deliberately not forced complements so the decomposes-rather-than-survives region stays reachable | shipped | high | [The Crucible metaplan](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-the-crucible-metaplan-design.md) |
| ALCH-4 | **The mundane tier ships ungated; the metaphysics gate is one predicate.** [[UNI-2]] asks whether magic is a second physics; this program does not open it and does not need to, because [frontier §magic](frontier.md#magic-as-a-graph-grammar--the-debt-economy) already argues superstition is the universal and magic is the special case where superstition happens to be *right*. A world with an empty violation catalog still derives correspondence-thinking, false causes, rival schools, and lost arts. **A production is a production whether or not it violates an enforced invariant**, so opening the gate later changes `permits` and nothing else. Reserved discard: a world with *no* consistent material rules at all — alchemy genuinely impossible, yet schools still form — a coherent tier-0 draw | raw | med | [The Crucible metaplan §5.4](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-the-crucible-metaplan-design.md) |
| ALCH-5 | **Alchemy is religion's fallible sibling.** Surfaced by negating "the doctrine can be wrong": that branch yields practitioners with oracular access, which is *revelation, not inference*, and `domains/religion` already occupies it. Alchemy takes the inference branch — a practitioner who samples, and can therefore be wrong. The phenomena seam (a consumer must never learn which system produced an observation) is unchanged by the whole program, and no campaign in it may weaken it. **Admissibility is not truth**: a doctrine validator asks whether a doctrine accounts for the observations its holder has *made*, never whether it is correct — collapsing the two would delete the subject matter in one line | raw | high | [The Crucible metaplan §5.3, §5.6](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-the-crucible-metaplan-design.md) |
| ALCH-7 | **Latent qualities, manifest signs — the split that makes the confound possible.** A substance's qualities are *latent*: a practitioner never reads composition directly, but perceives **signs** — weak, partly misleading functions of the qualities — plus reaction outcomes. Surfaced by asking whether the idea is public or hidden, and it **overturned [[ALCH-2]]'s first mitigation**, which had required qualities to be *observable*: if they were, there would be no confound and the program would have no subject matter. The constraint is *inferable*, not observable — every quality must affect at least one observable. The payoff is that `hue` can be made a deliberately weak function of the quality vector, which mechanizes the historical **doctrine of signatures** ("the root is red, so it treats blood") as a derivable error rather than an authored superstition. Reserved knob, not adopted: drawing the quality→sign projection *per world*, which would make signatures genuinely right in some worlds — cheap and powerful, but arbitrary rather than derived. Historical anchor for the whole confound: **wootz steel**, a lost art whose recipe depended on trace vanadium in one ore body, which died when that body was exhausted and has never been reconstructed. Shipped in The Reagent: `hue = 0.50·causticity + 0.45·vitality`, so a caustic mineral and an inert living thing both present 0.45 exactly — pinned by a test carrying an instruction not to repair it | shipped | high | [The Reagent spec §2](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-the-reagent-design.md) |
| ALCH-6 | **Doctrine accuracy is an ordinal lab metric — and the scale runs past its own maximum.** Positions: *signature* (a cause with zero predictive power) → *confounded* (a real correlate mistaken for the cause) → *overreached* (right cause, wrong scope) → *unmodified* (missing dose/purity/temperature) → *true production* (indistinguishable from the sim's rule; this position is called "science") → **accreted**, past 100%: a doctrine naming *more* conditions than the truth has. Precision without accuracy, and the mechanism behind ritual accretion — **a doctrine can be worse than wrong by being over-specified.** Preregisterable hypothesis for The Signature: doctrine accuracy varies inversely with the terrain heterogeneity an alchemist can reach — flat worlds converge on truth, fractured worlds hold doctrines at *confounded* and proliferate schools. **Constraint measured in The Reagent, to settle BEFORE this preregisters:** reachable-production count is a weak discriminator by construction — four ubiquitous source categories cover the whole seven-entry table, so every default-pin seed reaches all seven and between-world variance is ZERO. The hypothesis is untestable if exposure is "the world's reachable production set." Two fixes: measure reach LOCALLY (a settlement catchment, not a globe), and use a finer measure — distinct material categories, or ore-grade dispersion, the latter being the confound's actual mechanism and exactly what a production-set measure discards | raw | med | [The Crucible metaplan §6](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-the-crucible-metaplan-design.md) |

## Rendering — the observation stack

The rendering-strategy spec
([2026-07-09](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-rendering-strategy-design.md))
places every render on a four-ring axis (text in process → committed
artifacts → scene descriptions → external clients) under decision 0022's
seam: sim emits data, clients render. Rows here are the speculative rings;
the PNG migration stays TOOL-6, and the star chart is constitutionally
promised work (§3.4), not speculation.

| ID       | Idea                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Status | Conf | Where                                                                                     |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| RENDER-1 | Scene-description protocol — `windows/scene`, semantic-only JSON over the query surface (what an observer sees, never how to draw it; no producer identity); cartographic pole (tile lattice — where "tilemaps" lives) and situated pole (observer at a place and time — the phenomena protocol serialized); schemas are save-format-class contracts. **The situated pole was BUILT 2026-07-26** (campaign *The Purview*, [[RENDER-4]]'s first rung): `scene/surrounds/v1`, the sixth scene kind and the first egocentric one — and the first to carry an *epistemic* field, since a situated document describes what an observer knows, not merely what is there | shipped | high | [scene-protocol spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-scene-protocol-design.md)        |
| RENDER-2 | In-book web viewer — the atlas: a TypeScript client under `clients/` (decision 0023), unit-tested, bundled to a committed `atlas.js`; five layers, hover readout, markers, pan/zoom over the committed scene JSON; sky-scrubbing awaits a situated-pole scene kind | shipped | med  | [atlas-viewer spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-atlas-viewer-design.md) |

Nearly-free mechanism: an absence is legible only against an expectation, and the fields ARE the prior while the ledger is reality — so a *salient absence = where the field-prior expects something the ledger lacks* (coarse-constrains-fine run as a difference, not a constraint), a lacunae query beside phenomena, rendered by the focalizer as felt gaps. This is the phenomena rule aimed at the view layer — a consumer must never learn which system produced a phenomenon; a viewer is never handed unmediated sight — and it makes the caption, not the picture, the load-bearing honesty: what a lens exaggerates or invents is stated, because nothing on screen is exempt from having been *chosen*. ### The orrery atlas — enrichment directions

A 2026-07-10 ideonomy pass over the then-shipped live orrery (RENDER-5:
`scene/system/v1` + `clients/orrery/`) — dimension-identification along
cardinality, visibility, and size, then combination against the sim's other
surfaces (the almanac, the atlas, the Lab, the SKY atlas above), captured as
a graph. The in-book client the pass targeted is gone: the [Goldengrove
spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-goldengrove-design.md)
retired the terminal and live orreries in favor of an external 3D client
over the versioned wasm catalog, which inherits every row below. The
graph's two hubs, which price every row: **the scene schema**
(about half the rows widen `scene/system/v1`, and any widening that adds
client-side physics must extend the two-language golden-sample contract that
pins the TypeScript ephemeris to the sim), and **the time axis** (the
scrubber owns one year; several rows contend for a second, longer clock).
Rows needing neither — pure consumers of data the client already holds — are
the cheapest real enrichment, and **Conf** reads as in the SKY atlas: *how
cheap and clearly-correct the work is*. IDs are category+slug per decision
[`0026-slugs-not-numbers`](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0026-slugs-not-numbers.md).

| ID | Idea | Status | Conf | Where |
| -- | ---- | ------ | ---- | ----- |

| MAP-perceive-apertures | Look-direction perception through apertures — `look <dir>` renders a *neighbouring* locale as perception actually delivers it (a distance-attenuated, aperture-filtered **exterior** view — "to the north, past the tree-line, a darker wood, and faint water beyond") rather than reciting the room's first-person self-description (the MUD/ZIL vantage failure). Model: `perceived(feature) = carry(feature, channel) × transmit(aperture, channel) × falloff(distance)`, thresholded, confidence ∝ the margin above threshold — a spatial per-channel extension of the salience-`observe` fold, not new machinery. Four channels penetrate differently (a lattice): **sight** (blocked by occlusion/darkness), **light** (a glow through trees; enhanced at night), **sound** (bends around edges), **atmosphere** (weather/temperature — [[CLIM-felt-weather]]'s phenomena — pervade) — so *dense forest at night* yields hear+feel+glow but no sight, truer than any MUD. View = backdrop (pervasive features) + details (point features, if transmitted). Uncertainty is the currency that closes cognition: a hedged glimpse → low-confidence belief (the-surmise's tier) → the planner treats it as a hypothesis to verify (the-foresight targets belief) → a closer look self-corrects. The dormant `PerceptionVector` (night-vision) gets its first job (same aperture, different observer); *being seen is the dual of seeing* (stealth/exposure, later). A pure lens (decision 0022 — read-only, non-deterministic-OK, zero save-format cost). 2 ideonomy passes, 0 overturns. | elaborated | high (fun) | design companion (this session); [The Locale Window](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-12-the-locale-window-design.md) |
| MAP-connectors-as-apertures | Exits as derived-or-declared apertures, never imperative — replaces the ZIL/Inform `room \| function \| fail-message` union, whose `function` variant maximizes flexibility at the cost of navigability/transparency/mapping (an opaque closure you can't inspect, render, or reason over). Hornvale's line: **derive** (a pure function of the world — inspectable, explainable) or **declare** (authored data), never imperative code. The union collapses: `Room(dest)` → the aperture's destination attribute; `FailMessage(str)` → the *body* channel's transmission = 0 with a **derived Reason** ("sheer cliff", "flooded at this tide", "barred") the world explains; `Function` → deleted, its jobs split into derived transmission (conditional passability), a declarative `Portal` connector (computed destination, as data), and a separate action (side-effects). Load-bearing collapse: **an exit *is* an aperture — passability is the `body` channel of the same `transmit(aperture, channel)` [[MAP-perceive-apertures]] uses** (a wall stops body+sight; a river stops body not sight; a doorway passes both). A connection is a symmetric **edge** between two rooms (a Fact-shaped relation), not a room-owned slot; transmission is per-direction only where it differs (a cliff: descend-not-climb). Authored connectors are a **closed, registered vocabulary** (Door/Portal/Gate/Bridge…), bounded not open-ended (the closed-inventory pattern). **Opens a large unexplored area — buildings, vehicles, boats, interiors are all connectors + authored spaces** (the `ExitKind` extension point in `windows/locale` is pre-shaped for it); parked as too broad for the cognition work. Open sub-questions: derived-vs-stored (a derived aperture is a pure view; is an authored Door a Fact or dungeon data?); the connector vocabulary; the transmission function's terrain inputs. 3 ideonomy passes, 0 overturns (organon×negation → exit-as-edge, uniform-not-union, discover-by-default/invent-sparsely, bounded-complexity). | raw | high | design session (this conversation) |

### The game client atlas — the multi-pane program

A 2026-07-25 brainstorm plus two ideonomy passes (abstraction-lift and
dimension-identification, captured as an atlas; then substitution and
combination, captured as a timeline) over the question of a **multi-pane
browser game client** — focalized prose beside a top-down view of the
immediate room beside health/status — built on the Casement's wasm seam
([decision 0052](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0052-deploy-built-wasm.md)),
TS-authored and JS-shipped under `clients/` per
[decision 0023](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0023-in-repo-clients-carry-their-own-toolchains.md).
Herbert Wolverson's Rust roguelike tutorial supplied the feature checklist
the second pass crossed against Hornvale's own mechanisms
([[CLIENT-coverage-matrix]]).

Costs were **measured before designing** (native release plus a Node bench
over the Casement ABI, one box, medians): a game-scale turn tick costs
**4.75 ms** in wasm, a movement turn 1.15 ms, a `locale` room describe
0.010 ms native — against a 16.7 ms frame. Frame rate is a non-question: the
sim sits in a Worker, off the frame thread, and is turn-driven, so it
contributes zero frame time. Two numbers do bind. A *simulated day* costs
516 ms, and integrating at six-second granularity costs 68,386 ms per
simulated day against bulk advance's 516 — a 130× penalty for resolution
that reproduces [[UNI-32]]'s presence-induces-integration thesis from the
cost side, unprompted ([[CLIENT-four-clocks]]). And cold start is 3.6–5.0 s,
the one red budget ([[CLIENT-cold-start]]).

Three hubs price every row. **The two-tier position law**
([[CLIENT-two-tier-position]]) is load-bearing over all of it and is
Nathan's, not the passes': an entity's *persisted* position is its room; a
tile coordinate exists only inside the presence bubble and is never
serialized. **The snapshot contract** ([[CLIENT-one-snapshot]]) prices the
panes — nearly every row is a pane, and a pane is a pure projection of one
per-turn emit, so the schema is the only thing expensive to get wrong. And
**authority** ([[CLIENT-room-grid-authority]]) settles what the sim must emit
versus what the client may invent, which is where this program stops being
"a client" and becomes producer-side work.

Scope resolves into three nested rungs with three representations, not the
single "room scale" the first pass assumed: the **settlement** carries a
creature's home range (persisted — the goblins who do not wander out of the
village), the **room** carries `agent-at` and is the *commit granularity*,
and the **tile** is the transient bubble interior that is never persisted.
`Facet { face, path }` already spans the top two — a "room" is a leaf, a
"floor" or chunk is a path prefix at some depth — so the ambiguity is in the
word, not the model ([[CLIENT-tiles-as-deeper-rooms]] asks whether the tile
is simply a longer path). **Conf** reads as in
the SKY and orrery atlases: how cheap and clearly-correct the work is. IDs
are category+slug per decision 0026's still-standing registry provision
(0043 superseded only its decision-record clause).

| CLIENT-prose-primacy | **A permanently visible map pane demotes prose, through layout rather than through any ratified decision.** **RESOLVED (Amendment 1, 2026-07-25) by adopting [[CLIENT-relational-fine-layer]] + [[CLIENT-alive-map]]:** prose and picture become two renderings of ONE relational structure, so they cannot compete as rival accounts, and the map carries no truth claim (it is the agent's remembered artifact). The resolution came from restating the interface's PURPOSE — substrate for linguistic / economic / behavioural complexity, not tactical play — which showed the grid was answering an unasked question. [[CLIENT-discovery-pane]] is additive, not a resolution; [[CLIENT-as-instrument]] remains open. The polarity flip on "more panes, more legibility": Constitution §3.5 makes focalized prose primary and the tilemap secondary, and [[RENDER-4]]'s own row says so in as many words — yet every roguelike player's eye goes to the grid, and layout is not a preference the constitution can enforce. So the browser turn is ~1.8 ms and the emit ~2.2 ms, comfortably under the 4.75 ms floor. What that campaign *did* measure is the world clock's neighbour, not this one: the health battery, the longest sim in the suite, ran 250.65 s against a 266.36 s baseline, so the restructure of the sim's hottest loop cost nothing in bulk advance. | CLIENT-tiles-as-deeper-rooms | **Is a tile simply a longer `Facet` path?** **REJECTED (The Rose Window Amendment 1, 2026-07-25).** Not for the quadtree-neighbour cost, which is survivable, but because a tile would then be the SAME RUST TYPE as a room — so a tile position would be expressible wherever a room position is, including `AGENT_AT`, and [[CLIENT-two-tier-position]]'s "byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION" would degrade to by-policy (risk 4, persistence-tier drift, goes from impossible to merely policed).
