## Narrative delivery — which piece next

A 2026-07-31 ideonomy session over Emily Short's 2016 survey of quality-based,
salience-based and waypoint narrative structures — nine passes of operators
(negation, substitution, combination, abstraction-lift, cross-domain
re-instantiation, tree-finding) against a taxonomy that explicitly brackets
simulation out. These rows index the imports and the two negative results; the
argument is one [frontier section](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived).
Delivery is the **rendering cluster's prose sibling**: RENDER-\* answers how a
thing is rendered, this answers in what order it arrives.

| ID | Idea | Status | Conf | Where |
| -- | ---- | ------ | ---- | ----- |
| NARR-delivery | The six policies — delivery decomposes into selection, piece-boundary, ordering, rate, repetition and refusal, and the craft literature's three canonical structures are all *selection* policies, exhausting one branch of six. Prose delivery is the **sixth readout**, sibling to the shipped chart (spatial), almanac (documentary), census (statistical), ephemeris (predictive) and `explain` trace (causal) — so it belongs in the derived-view architecture, not a subsystem of its own | elaborated | high | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-idempotence | **The diagnosis: pull + idempotent.** Delivery varies on two independent bits — initiative (player pulls vs world pushes) and reversibility (spent vs re-deliverable). Every window here is a repeatable query, which is why a generated world reads as an encyclopedia rather than a story; all three craft structures are push+spent, diagonally opposite. The content lifecycle has **no `spent` state** — `delivered` returns to `offered`. One missing state and one missing policy, not a subsystem | elaborated | high | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-attention-budget | Attention is the scarce resource; content is not — the inversion that makes craft advice non-transferable at the root. Authored content is scarce and attention abundant (craft = selection); derived content is unbounded and attention bounded (craft = budgeting). The usable precedent is [[MAP-62]]'s keystone — salience-budgeted feature selection per zoom, ratified for map symbols, never pointed at prose. Sources are distributed but the rank is concentrated at one merge: the policy has exactly one seat | elaborated | high | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-rotation | Coverage by rotation, not ranking — salience-ranking starves low-salience content forever, while a lectionary's fixed cycle guarantees the corpus is seen. **Scoped to the exhibition tier, not the collection:** on an axis of fraction-ever-surfaced a walked world sits near 0.001%, the target is a museum's ~1%, and 99%-in-storage is not a failure — so this is selection *quality* at tiny coverage, not a coverage problem. The axis extends past 100% into fabrication, where rumour and error live | elaborated | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-piece-size | Let form fix the size, offline — the lectionary's *pericope* settles excerpt boundaries once by committee; oral-formulaic composition picks the epithet that fits the metrical slot. Two eras, the same answer independently: size is decided by form *before* delivery, never per-delivery | raw | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-altitude | The label hierarchy — a museum shows object label, wall panel, room text and catalogue *simultaneously* and lets the visitor choose depth, which beats picking an altitude per delivery. Offer every scale at once and let attention descend; read that way, `explain` stops being a derivation dump and becomes a depth ladder. The prose analogue of the zoom rungs the map already has | elaborated | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-drift | An arc without authoring one — delivery today is temporally *steady*; the other temporal directions give a backlog (accumulating), content that rots unseen (decaying), alternating registers (oscillating), and **drift**: a monotone over the salience weighting across a session. The cheapest dramatic shape — no beat, no destination — and free because it lives in a lens (decision 0022). Its sibling is the callback, whose value depends on session position, not world state | elaborated | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-drifting-waypoint | The drifting waypoint — crossing waypoint narrative with salience dissolves the authored-beat objection: the story still heals toward a destination, but the destination is *drawn from the world* rather than written. [[MAP-14]]'s fate rigidity (draw either the outcome or the path, derive the other in one pass) is that same mechanism reached from metaphysics instead of craft — independent convergence on an already-elaborated row | raw | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-refusal | Refusal is a delivery act — the craft structures differ most in the column nobody discusses: a greyed-out locked storylet, silence, and a fallback line are three genuinely distinct designs for absence, and [[RENDER-7]] has no vocabulary for the distinction. Reading delivery's side effect as its main effect adds the prerequisite never written down: a salient absence is illegible until enough presence has been delivered for it to violate | elaborated | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-placed-content | The storylet's native form is a place, not a card — give content physical embodiment (an inscription, a scar, a ruin) and the gate stops being a quality check and becomes *being there*. The delivery index is then the room mesh, which already carries a purview and a fog model, making spendable placed content far cheaper than a storylet engine | raw | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-monument-writes-itself | A monument is placed content whose text the world can derive — the concrete instance [[NARR-placed-content]] asks for. Who it commemorates is committed history; what it says is the language engine at that register ([[EXP-7]]); whether you can read it is literacy plus tongue-distance, so erosion yields a PARTIAL reading rather than a coin flip; how worn it is is age against material. What it omits is the sharp part, since a monument is erected by a winner. Rendering, not authoring, is the whole cost | elaborated | high | [frontier §place-with-users](frontier.md#the-place-with-users--what-a-dungeon-feature-is-not) |
| NARR-lifecycle | The content lifecycle is [[PSY-5]]'s machine pointed at the player — *latent → noticed → held → expressed → transmitted → ritualized*, already specified for an idea inside a creature. Two findings fall out: `stale → delivered` is legal and load-bearing (memory, rumour, error), and entering *taken up* is **unverifiable** — nothing can observe whether a reader understood, which is why rotation beats modelling uptake. Corrected — the player *does* have a checked knowledge store ([[KNOW-observer-built]]); what is absent is [[UNI-16]]'s threshold | elaborated | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-emit-boundary | Narration is an emit boundary — delivery lifted free of craft vocabulary is lossy compression of world state into a rate-limited serial channel, structurally identical to serialization. Decision 0033's quantize-at-emit-only rule therefore carries an exact narrative reading: **never let what you are going to narrate change what happens.** The anti-*Façade* rule, already constitutional in another register | elaborated | high | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-derived-quest | A quest is a path through the precondition graph — crossing quality-based gating with waypoint pathfinding yields a route toward a locked storylet with its intermediate gates made legible, which is what "quest" structurally means. Buildable over the ledger by pathfinding toward a fact the player wants true, using the planning engine's A-star across the tenses. The unordered-prerequisites-then-gate pattern is free in a sim; only the gate needs authoring | raw | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-delivery-study | The delivery layer has never been measured — Short notes such a system could be validated by thousands of randomized playthroughs visualizing which sequences never fire and which are overused. That instrument exists here (the Laboratory, census scale, metrics as code, preregistered studies) and has never been pointed at delivery. Coverage, dominance (which phenomenon kind heads every world's ranking) and pacing are metrics, not features — the rung that makes the rest admissible | raw | high | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-hook | The hook is the one irreducible authored thing — situation-based prep dissolves every failure point except the first, the reason to engage at all, which the prep literature names as shared by every scenario and unremovable by any amount of prep. In a derived world everything else derives; motivation does not. It is [[NARR-attention-budget]]'s thesis reached from the prep side rather than the delivery side, and it bounds what a knowability field ([[KNOW-field]]) can buy: *reachable* is not *wanted* | raw | med | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-crawl-goal | `possess` is a hexcrawl carrying the one default goal the form's own history says fails. `go` gives a default action and a closed loop, and locales are firewalled — four of the five parts of a complete scenario structure. The fifth, a default *goal*, is bare exploration, which the tabletop record blames for hexcrawling's collapse: no motivation, no reward. No goal verb, no reward of any kind. Evidence for [[NARR-hook]], and it names the remedy others reached for — graft a specific goal (discovery bounties, West Marches) rather than invent one | raw | high | `possess` verb list; [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-neglect-bounty | The accumulating neglect bounty — a third answer to starvation, and better than either standing option. *Puerto Rico* adds a coin to any role nobody took, every turn, until someone cannot resist: reward the neglected rather than penalise the favoured. Applied to selection, unshown content accrues a monotone bonus that clears when shown — deterministic, O(1) per item, no cycle bookkeeping, and eventual coverage without [[NARR-rotation]]'s fixed lectionary or a ranker's permanent starvation. Its transparency mattered too: players were told the rule up front | raw | med | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (game-economy design); [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-discovery-ledger | The cross-run discovery ledger — the reward [[NARR-crawl-goal]] lacks, and the one the roguelike genre actually converged on. Cogmind's gallery records every item ever found with a usage count, and its stated value is showing *how much more there is to discover*: cumulative, legible, a motive for exploration rather than a graft onto it. It costs no world mutation, so it survives the discarded session [[KNOW-monotone]] leaves amnesiac across runs, and it is the player-facing face of the coverage quantity [[NARR-neglect-bounty]] tracks from the other side | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (roguelike morgue files); [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-ordering-not-choice | A non-exclusive corpus offers ordering, not choice — the talent-tree critique, and it is [[NARR-idempotence]] arriving from character progression. If taking A never forecloses B the only decision is sequence; synergy worsens it by collapsing many options into two real lines, and prerequisites push the first real choice out to the tips. Delivery here is pull and idempotent — ask twice, receive twice, `delivered` returning to `offered` — so *which piece next* is the only lever it has, which is why the missing `spent` state is load-bearing rather than a detail | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (magic-system redux); [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-sliding-window | The sliding window — a bounded contiguous slice of an *ordered* corpus, advancing monotonically, sized to the mind's limit on simultaneous choice. Its source draws (10×9)^12 configurations from 120 abilities ordered by power, which no tree of that size matches. As a selection policy it is the third sibling to [[NARR-rotation]]'s fixed cycle and [[NARR-neglect-bounty]]'s accruing bonus, and the only one needing an order — which [[KNOW-substrate]] already supplies as topological order over the derivation graph | raw | med | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (magic-system redux); [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-neglect-consequence | Neglect can be paid in salience or in consequence, and only one is free. [[NARR-neglect-bounty]] raises unshown content's *rank*, which lives in a lens and costs nothing (decision 0022). Raising its *stakes* — the unvisited threat that grows because you left it — changes the world, so it must stay a function of seed and elapsed time. Within a session that is available, since the ledger clone holds the play; across sessions it is not, because the clone is discarded ([[UNI-play-persistence]]), so a world can never know what you skipped last time | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (the 5-node mystery); [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-retrospective-climax | The climax is an extremum over the trajectory, named at emit. Skip the prepared finale and whatever you *did* meet becomes the climax — assigned by the path, not the design. [[NARR-drifting-waypoint]] draws its destination in advance and steers toward it, which brushes [[NARR-emit-boundary]]'s rule that narration must never change what happens; naming the peak *afterwards* cannot, so it is strictly safer and free. [[MAP-metric-temporality]]'s extremal class pointed at narrative, and the argmax belongs in [[UNI-run-record]] | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (the 5-node mystery); [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-structural-tell | Recognition of content comforts; recognition of *structure* deadens — the caveat [[KNOW-recognition-floor]] needs. A fixed five-room template yields effective material and predictable material at once, and the tell is the skeleton rather than the furniture. So a recognition floor built by repeating *templates* backfires where one built by revisiting *places* does not, and the exposure count at which a skeleton becomes legible is small. Distinct from [[MAP-29]]'s oatmeal problem, which is variety of content, not detectability of shape | raw | med | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (the 5-node mystery); [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |
| NARR-endogenous-corpus | The world can generate its own corpus, which is the real answer to [[NARR-corpus-provenance]]. Eponymy ([[LANG-eponym]]) coins categories from memorable instances, so a culture accumulates named situations nobody imported — and those are the *right* hypothesis space for [[UNI-abduction]], since a drow recognises through drow concepts and not Polti's. Keep both: the external corpus measures reach, the endogenous one measures what this world found worth naming, and the disagreement is the finding | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (eponymy, the Glorg manoeuvre) |
| NARR-corpus-provenance | No corpus speaks for the world, so the instrument carries provenance and the output is a matrix rather than a score. Polti is 1895 French dramaturgy, Propp is Russian folktale, TVTropes is contemporary anglophone media — each a labelled probe of known bias, none an inventory of the possible, which is [[PSY-five-is-lexical]]'s error one domain over. That needs a third verdict beside satisfied and missing: **`inapplicable(reason)`**, for a situation presupposing what this world deliberately lacks. No marriage, so no "Adultery" — different, not deficient | ratified (0095) | high | [decision 0095](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0095-a-corpus-is-an-instrument-never-a-standard.md); [The Repertoire](../chronicle/the-repertoire.md) + [The Collation](../chronicle/the-collation.md) chronicles |
| NARR-three-columns | Expressible splits three ways and each wants different machinery. *Representable*: the fact can exist — registry tokens, checkable today. *Generable*: an agent can form the goal and plan it — GOAP over belief, which The Surmise ships, plus [[PSY-5]] for conceiving what was never held. *Recognisable*: an agent can infer it happened from what it left — [[UNI-abduction]], absent. The three diverge, and the divergences are the interesting worlds: crimes nobody can solve, detectives with nothing to detect | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (tropes as capability probes) |
| NARR-trope-as-probe | Run the trope backwards and it becomes a coverage probe rather than content. An ambitious drow framing a superior for murder is not a thing to generate; it is a *conjunction of required mechanisms* — ambition, a hierarchy worth climbing, killing classified as murder, forged evidence, others who credit it, a sanction, a vacancy. [[UNI-21]] already proposes the compiled capability set; a trope corpus is the query language over it, asked in the demand direction. The fraction mechanically possible is one censusable number for expressive range | shipped | high | [The Repertoire](../chronicle/the-repertoire.md) |
| NARR-mechanism-leverage | Decomposition yields a prioritisation function nobody has to argue about. If each trope is a conjunction of mechanisms then each mechanism carries a fan-in — how many situations require it — and the backlog sorts itself: ambition earns its place because forty scenarios need it, not because it sounds good. That inverts feature-driven ordering, and the counts are computed from the decomposition graph rather than debated. Measured, fan-in ranks leverage but is *not* an unlock count. [[NARR-trope-as-probe]]'s corpus is the input | shipped | high | [The Repertoire](../chronicle/the-repertoire.md) |
| NARR-reachable-vs-possible | Engine-capability and agent-reachability are different things, and [[UNI-21]] runs them together. It says GOAP's available-action set *is* a capability query — true of what the engine can represent, false of what an agent can conceive. A world may fully support framing while no drow ever has the idea, because plan search ranges only over operators already held. [[PSY-5]]'s invention machinery is the bridge, so a trope wants two checks: can the world represent it, and can a mind reach it | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (tropes as capability probes) |
| NARR-demand-side-scan | The trope corpus is the demand-side scan, and [[UNI-21]] already holds the supply side. That row turns orphan predicates and unconsumed phenomena into a self-query — mechanisms nothing needs, which [[TOOL-graph-defects]] calls *Nothing*. Decomposed tropes ask the opposite: needs that no mechanism serves, a *Broken Link*. Run together they close a loop, and either alone is half a check, since an engine can be at once full of unused capability and unable to stage its own genre | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (tropes as capability probes) |
| NARR-trope-graphs | What transfers from trope-graph narrative generation, and what does not. Not the generation half: a trope graph is a *plot*, and [[KNOW-no-mandatory-node]] already establishes that a world requiring nothing has no derailment to insure against, so no node must be delivered. What transfers is the evaluation half — the defect vocabulary ([[TOOL-graph-defects]]) and the archive ([[MAP-qd-archive]]) — plus the authors' own caution that structural coherence is explicitly not story quality | raw | high | ideonomy session 2026-07-31 (TropeTwist, Alvarez & Font 2022) |
| NARR-action-economy | **Rejected: the action economy.** Fallen London's regenerating-actions rate limiter is the most obvious import from quality-based narrative and the wrong one — it is shaped by monetization rather than craft, metering attention against a manufactured scarcity. Recorded because someone will propose it; the rate policy wants a real answer ([[NARR-drift]], [[NARR-rotation]]) instead | rejected | — | [frontier §delivery](frontier.md#narrative-delivery--which-piece-next-when-content-is-derived) |

## Knowability — whether a piece can be reached at all

A 2026-07-31 ideonomy session over Justin Alexander's node-based scenario
design — eight passes of operators (negation, substitution, abstraction-lift,
cross-domain re-instantiation, tree-finding, combination) against a tabletop
prep discipline for situations. The argument is one
[frontier section](frontier.md#knowability--whether-a-derived-world-can-be-known-from-inside-it).
Knowability is [[NARR-delivery]]'s **topological sibling**: NARR-\* answers in
what order content arrives, RENDER-\* how it is rendered, this whether it is
reachable at all. Load-bearing correction inside: the player observer model the
delivery cluster records as absent is substantially built.

| ID | Idea | Status | Conf | Where |
| -- | ---- | ------ | ---- | ----- |
| KNOW-field | The knowability field — negating node-discreteness leaves a gradient rather than keyed locations: a scalar field over the world giving, at each point, how much of the world's truth is determinable from there. Fields are already the kernel's third trace primitive, so this is derivable, byte-identical, renderable by the machinery that writes an elevation map, and censusable at census scale. **Discovered, not invented** — a property the world has whether or not anyone computes it, hence a readout, hence constitutionally free | elaborated | high | [frontier §knowability](frontier.md#knowability--whether-a-derived-world-can-be-known-from-inside-it) |
| KNOW-projection | Traversal is symmetric, deduction is not — Alexander's aside that dungeon geography reverses while mystery structure runs one way is the precise statement of the whole idea. Two structures are superimposed on every world here and have never been related to each other: the undirected room mesh you walk, and the directed acyclic derivation graph you reason along. **The knowability field is the projection of the DAG onto the mesh** | elaborated | high | [frontier §knowability](frontier.md#knowability--whether-a-derived-world-can-be-known-from-inside-it) |
| KNOW-no-mandatory-node | The Three Clue Rule does not transfer, and that is the finding — it is explicit that it governs only conclusions a scenario *requires*, and a sim requires nothing, so there is no derailment to insure against and the rule's purpose evaporates on contact. What survives is the instrument rather than the rule: the GM's revelation list stops measuring "will the adventure survive" and starts measuring **how much of this world is knowable at all** | elaborated | high | [frontier §knowability](frontier.md#knowability--whether-a-derived-world-can-be-known-from-inside-it) |
| KNOW-closure | Three is closure, not redundancy — surveying's justification beats the rule author's own: three is the first count that detects inconsistency **without an external reference** (two agreeing measurements bound no error, three do). Closure is trivial under determinism unless traces can lie, so once forgery and rumour exist the shape of play is **find the inconsistency**, not find three clues. The position-blind sky is this world's benchmark network | elaborated | med | [frontier §knowability](frontier.md#knowability--whether-a-derived-world-can-be-known-from-inside-it) |
| KNOW-independence | Independence is disjoint derivation ancestry — three claims resting on one doctrine's authority are one claim. Exactly computable: two traces are independent iff their ancestries are disjoint, i.e. `explain` twice, intersected. Intelligence practice names the failure it prevents (**circular reporting** — two apparent sources, one origin, confidence inflated accordingly). Supplies [[MAP-2]] the *reason* it has always lacked: one provenance field, not a second ledger | spec'd | high | [frontier §knowability](frontier.md#knowability--whether-a-derived-world-can-be-known-from-inside-it) · [The Hearsay spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-the-hearsay-design.md) |
| KNOW-corroboration-needs-variation | **Corroboration is semantic, so a structural campaign cannot measure it — three proxies failed first.** It needs accounts that COULD differ; where content is carried unchanged, no two can disagree and every topological stand-in measures redundancy. Contact is NOT the precondition assumed: [[KNOW-contact-is-an-edge]] measured disagreement FALLING once a seam exists. **The cheapest belief route is dead too**: a concordant-telling count is what `frequency`/`frequency-w` already are (neither broke pooling), and under descent every holder gets ONE telling, so it is 1 where the seam is absent | raw | high | [The Hearsay spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-the-hearsay-design.md) · [The Parley chronicle](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/book/src/chronicle/the-parley.md) · [The Undertow chronicle](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/book/src/chronicle/the-undertow.md) |
| KNOW-divergence-antichain | **Divergent testimony is an antichain, and three near-misses were all the wrong object.** Corroboration is symmetric; ancestry is a partial order and antisymmetric by definition, so filtering a witness set by ancestry can never express it. The symmetric relation inside a partial order is INCOMPARABILITY, and a pairwise-incomparable witness set is an antichain. For witnesses {A, B, C} with B and C survivors of A, the maximum antichain is {B, C}; the minimal elements are {A}. Measure the former. Disjoint ancestries ([[KNOW-independence]]) is stronger still and drops the same survivors | shipped | high | [The Retelling chronicle](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/book/src/chronicle/the-retelling.md) |
| KNOW-lectio-difficilior | The harder reading is likelier original, and that is a falsifiable prediction about a census. Stemmatics holds *lectio difficilior potior*: copyists simplify, so of two variant readings the more surprising one sits closer to the archetype. Re-instantiated for myth — if retellings regularise, surviving variants should be measurably SIMPLER than the committed facts they descend from. It has a real null, because the folklore literature's competing claim is that retellings *elaborate*. Untestable until claims can mutate, so it is the diffusion campaign's headline, not [[KNOW-independence]]'s | raw | med | [The Hearsay spec §7](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-the-hearsay-design.md) |
| KNOW-antigenic-sin | Distortion as a first-hearing anchor rather than a random walk. Immunology's *original antigenic sin*: the body meets a new variant and answers it with memory of the FIRST one it ever saw, badly. Re-instantiated, a holder reads every later telling through the version it heard first, so distortion is a deterministic function of that holder's own acquisition history instead of a per-hop dice roll. Cheaper than a seeded walk — there is no walk state to persist — and compatible with belief-as-a-fold, which already sees acquisition order. Pairs with [[MEM-1]]'s melt path | raw | med | [The Hearsay spec §7](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-the-hearsay-design.md) |
| KNOW-two-filter-chain | **Transmission is two filters, not one mutation** — `producer -> productive filter -> receptive filter -> receiver`. What a teller ENCODES (keyed on its incentive) and what a hearer DECODES (keyed on its formation) are separate functions, so the same claim moving between different (teller, hearer) pairs is transformed differently and the variance is structured by the social graph rather than by an authored rate. Unifies [[KNOW-antigenic-sin]] (the receptive half) with perspective-at-hops-0 (the productive half). Deterministic, so a window may host it: no draw, no stream label, no epoch | shipped | high | [The Retelling chronicle](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/book/src/chronicle/the-retelling.md) |
| KNOW-mismatch-needs-contact | **Unmeasurable corroboration and blocked prejudice are ONE scarcity.** Accounts diverge only where [[KNOW-two-filter-chain]]'s filters mismatch; mismatch needs a boundary crossing, hence contact. Seed 42: **0/658** inheritance edges cross `occ-people`, 17/474 endings have a foreign witness. [[KNOW-corroboration-needs-variation]] and [[SOC-intramural-violence]] share a cause; a species-keyed filter is inert by construction. **Corrected by [[KNOW-contact-is-an-edge]]: the scarcity is the graph's, not the world's; the baseline is 19 mutually-exclusive events/12 seeds, not set inequality's 111** | shipped | high | [The Retelling chronicle](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/book/src/chronicle/the-retelling.md) · [The Parley chronicle](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/book/src/chronicle/the-parley.md) |
| KNOW-misattribution-drift | Distortion of the SUBJECT, not the object — *the raid we remember happened to our neighbours*. `Claim` carries six fields and every treatment of distortion so far drifts only `object`; subject-drift is misattribution, is dramatically richer, is exactly scoreable against the committed fact, and needs no numeric noise scale invented for it. ## Possession as progression — the game's spine

The rows above ask what can be *known*; these ask what can be *played*. The
cluster is one design: the player is an immaterial soul that sees the whole
world from the first minute, and the constraint on it is not visibility but
**accessibility** — landmarks legible immediately, reachable only after the
world's own knowledge has been walked toward them. Captured 2026-08-12 from a
brainstorm reading Breath of the Wild's landmark theory into a top-down
roguelike, and argued in [frontier §possession](frontier.md#possession-as-progression--how-a-soul-earns-the-right-to-be-somewhere).
The rows still marked `raw` are the ones that essay does not yet carry. The one
true blocker ([[PLAY-inheritance-blocker]]) is a single line of shipped code.

| ID | Idea | Status | Conf | Where |
|----|------|--------|------|-------|
| PLAY-retired-bare-form-hint | A bare group-A verb typed from habit gets an ordinary unknown-verb refusal, where it should get a hint. The Deed retired all seven bare operator instruments (`why` `npcs` `help` `eyes` `whoami` `provoke` `soothe`) for `!`-prefixed forms, and decision 0169 makes the sigil a NAMESPACE, so `why` no longer resolves at all. Deferred out of that arc explicitly. The refusal knows the verb exists in the other namespace and says nothing; "did you mean `!why`?" is a two-line lookup. The world REPL keeps bare `help`/`why`, so the two surfaces now spell one word differently | raw | med (UX) | The Deed |
| PLAY-durations-and-interruption | Durations and interruption: `Action::Rest` is a multi-day act modelled as ONE tick with a teleport to the wake moment, so the codebase has one long action and no CONCEPT of one, and no act can be interrupted by anything. The Deed made this visible by routing a player's `sleep` through the same machinery — a body that lies down during its waking phase wakes at the next 0.05-day scan step, and on a tidally-locked world always naps a fixed 0.05 days. Carried from The Tackle F-2. Wants a duration model before a finer sleep rule | raw | high (model) | The Deed |
| PLAY-driver-substitutability | A driver is a VISITOR over a creature, not a different kind of subject: keyboard, GOAP planner, script and future network peer are values of one parameter, and the creature is the subject in every case. **Shipped** by The Hand (Arc II of The Bridle), closing 0167's must-fix: `Npc` and `Agent` collapsed into one `Body` (0229), possession became a roster index rather than a mint (0227), and the source of intent became a `Controller` parameter `advance_one` never inspects (0228). `DefaultController` is a verified byte-identical pass-through. **A third driver shipped by The Coercion** (0336) | shipped | high (architecture) | [The Hand chronicle](../chronicle/the-hand.md); [The Coercion](../chronicle/the-coercion.md); [0228](../../../docs/decisions/0228-a-controller-is-a-parameter-of-the-tick.md); [0229](../../../docs/decisions/0229-one-body-type.md); [0167](../../../docs/decisions/0167-a-driver-is-interchangeable-and-a-possessed-body-is-a-creature.md) |
| PLAY-soul-progression | The game's spine — an immaterial soul sees the whole world from the first minute and is gated on where it has *been*, not what it knows: landmarks visible but not accessible. Synthesises [[UNI-18]], [[UNI-36]] and [[UNI-37]] | elaborated | high | [frontier §possession](frontier.md#possession-as-progression--how-a-soul-earns-the-right-to-be-somewhere) |
| PLAY-lit-is-known | Knowledge lights a place — the map shows what your vessels have heard of, which is what lets a distant city pull at you | elaborated | high | [frontier §possession](frontier.md#possession-as-progression--how-a-soul-earns-the-right-to-be-somewhere) |
| PLAY-no-reroll | The design principle behind the fixed start, and it generalises past this cluster: **variance belongs downstream of the first decision, never upstream of it.** A start that varies breeds save-scumming — the player rerolls for the run they wanted and the game becomes a slot machine played before it begins. Put the variance after the player has invested and scumming costs more than it returns. Names the failure mode Nethack's starting pet and DCSS's god choice both have, and rules it out by construction rather than by discipline | raw | high | brainstorm 2026-08-12 |
| PLAY-determinism-is-anti-scum | The constitution already supplies half of [[PLAY-no-reroll]] for free, and nobody has noticed. In a world that is a pure function of `(seed, pins)` there is **no random table to roll against**: reloading returns the identical world, so scumming reduces to *playing differently*, which is simply playing. Every variance a player could farm has to come from their own choices, which is exactly where [[PLAY-no-reroll]] wants it. A determinism guarantee adopted for byte-identity turns out to be a game-design property | raw | high | brainstorm 2026-08-12 |
| PLAY-fixed-cosmopolitan-start | The answer to what is lit at t=0: **every world opens in its flagship settlement**, a multicultural hub — that world's Baldur's Gate — with the starting room a market and the starting choice whoever is milling about buying things. Contact ([[PLAY-contact-not-hearsay]]) therefore begins as the hub and its surrounds; everything else is visible and shut. A seed with no such hub is unplayable, which [[PLAY-possession-r0]] should score | raw | high | brainstorm 2026-08-12 |

## Astronomy — the sky's near-term deficits

The astronomy domain (Campaign 2) is physically honest but **frozen and
place-less**: nothing in the sky evolves over `WorldTime` beyond calendar
phase, and there is no latitude or solar position. These rows capture the
near-term deficits — missing bodies, discarded physics, and static values that
need not be static — from a 2026-07-08 audit of the domain. SEQ-4/SEQ-5 hold
the observation-path (place-less-observer) half; these hold the
celestial-mechanics half. The **Conf** tag here reads as *how cheap and
clearly-correct the fix is*, not essay maturity — most reuse quantities the
model already computes. All point at the Campaign 2 spec's model card (§5), the
derived/approximated/drawn card each deficit extends.

| ID     | Idea                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Status | Conf | Where                                                                                     |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SKY-1  | Nothing in the sky evolves — **the moving-sky core shipped in Firm Ground II**: obliquity, eccentricity, and axial precession are now functions of `WorldTime` (`forcing.rs` `OrbitalForcing`, carrying SKY-2/4/21), and Deep Time (MAP-6) consumes them. The row's residual is now closed: **secular stellar brightening shipped in The Long Count** (`star.rs` `brightening_per_gyr`, a Sol-calibrated b = 0.10·M^2.5 per Gyr law, kin to SKY-13); semi-major-axis migration beyond the Milankovitch triad is **declined** (decision 0054) — disk-driven migration ends before a stable habitable world exists, and an isolated planet's post-genesis secular drift is effectively zero on every timescale the sim expresses. The original "MAP-6 has almost nothing to read" gap is closed | shipped | high | [Campaign 2 spec §5](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-05-campaign-2-the-sky-design.md); [Firm Ground II spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-firm-ground-ii-design.md); [decision 0054](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0054-no-orbital-migration.md) |
| SKY-2  | Obliquity is the *only* seasonal driver and orbits are perfectly circular (`calendar.rs` `daylight_fraction`; spec §5 declared approximation), so a zero-tilt world has *zero* seasonal variation. A single drawn **eccentricity** adds apsidal seasons — a second, tilt-independent driver giving even a zero-tilt world a year — and feeds MAP-6                                                                                                                    | shipped    | high | [Firm Ground II spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-firm-ground-ii-design.md)         |
| SKY-3  | Tidal-lock probability is a flat 5% (`anchor.rs`, `lock_roll < 0.05`), independent of orbit distance and stellar mass — yet locking is almost entirely proximity × mass. ### The enrichment atlas — substitutions beyond the deficit audit

A 2026-07-10 ideonomy pass over the domain — substitution along five
dimensions (hierarchy, homogeneity, distribution, visibility, polarity) —
generating enrichment directions rather than deficit fixes. IDs are
category+slug per decision
[`0026-slugs-not-numbers`](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0026-slugs-not-numbers.md).
**Conf** reads as in the deficit table: *how cheap and clearly-correct the
work is*. The visibility-dimension rows (seasonal-night-sky,
heliacal-risings, circumpolar, stale-alignments) are pure consumers of
data already drawn and currently decorative — the cheapest real
enrichment in the domain.

SKY-16 restructures the top of the sky’s tree; this restructures the middle — a pin-grade regime | raw | med | this conversation; ideonomy session |

### Exotic system architectures — the cells the model does not occupy

A 2026-07-16 sweep of **real, observed** system architectures against the
shape of astronomy's draw. The finding is uncomfortable, and worth stating
once rather than thirteen times: **reality is stranger than the model**.
Hornvale generates exactly one cell of the configuration space — one star,
one terrestrial anchor, N moons — while nearly every row below is a
configuration the solar system or the Kepler catalogue *already ships*.
(The Reckoning, later the same day, moved the moon clause off its own
deficit list: a moon now draws a formation mechanism, so N is no longer
uniformly small-regular-prograde — a `Capture` moon can be alien in
density, decoupled in age, and irregular enough to be retrograde. The
single-star, single-anchor cell is the deficit that remains.) "Strange new
worlds" is therefore not a licence to fabricate; it is a mandate to catch
up, and the rows below are stated as deficits against observed fact, not as
invention.

Each row names **what it costs the model**, which is the part a future
reader actually needs. The tier boundary is the load-bearing distinction:

- **Additive** — new draws and streams behind existing shapes, no spine
  change; pin-grade work of the kind SKY-22 already proved.
- **Spine-breaking** — attacks `Anchor` being singular and `sky_of(world)`
  assuming one world with one sky. These are a **program**, not a campaign,
  and must never be costed as one.

Six of the thirteen configurations swept were **already banked** and are
deliberately not re-filed: rings and their Roche-limit origin
(`SKY-rings`), the circumbinary/Tatooine regime (SKY-16), the habitable
moon (`SKY-moon-world`), extreme obliquity (`SKY-extreme-obliquity`), and
retrograde rotation (SKY-22 — not merely banked but *shipped*). **Conf**
reads as in the atlas above: *how cheap and clearly-correct the work is* —
never how real the phenomenon is, since the physics of every row below is
observed.

| ID | Idea | Status | Conf | Where |
| -- | ---- | ------ | ---- | ----- |
| SKY-binary-planet | Two comparable-mass worlds about a barycenter **outside both bodies** — real: Pluto–Charon, which makes this configuration not exotic but simply absent. Mutually tidally locked, so each hangs *permanently motionless* in the other's sky, a disc close enough to show weather crossing it: a second inhabited surface you can watch a storm move over, and never once see rise. **Spine-breaking, and the sharpest case of it** — `Anchor` is singular by construction and `sky_of(world)` assumes one world with one sky, so this needs two anchors, a shared barycentric orbit, and a sky that knows which surface it is seen from. The tide, calendar, and eclipse machinery (SKY-5, SKY-6) all become two-ended. A program, not a campaign | raw | low | [frontier §map](frontier.md#the-frontier-map) |
| SKY-trojan-world | A second world sharing the anchor's orbit exactly, librating about L4/L5 sixty degrees ahead or behind — **observed at moon scale**: Tethys keeps both Telesto and Calypso. A sibling world at *identical* insolation and period that never approaches and never recedes. `SKY-resonances` already banks the 1:1 case as a *companion body* hanging sixty degrees from the sun; this row is its escalation — the co-orbital is a **world**, which is what makes it **spine-breaking** rather than one more wanderer draw (SKY-9). Two anchors again, but unlike `SKY-binary-planet` the two skies are near-identical and the two climates are the same climate, which makes this the cheapest honest probe of a two-anchor model | raw | low | [frontier §map](frontier.md#the-frontier-map) |
| SKY-horseshoe-pair | Co-orbitals that periodically **exchange orbits** — real, and not rare: Janus and Epimetheus trade every four years, the inner one catching the outer, swapping angular momentum, and becoming it. A neighbour world that closes for years, swaps places with you, then recedes for years: a clock nobody designed and no culture would have chosen, which is precisely the intercalation nightmare `SKY-calendar-hardness` exists to score. Additive if the co-orbital is a body (a wanderer whose distance beats on a decades-scale cycle); spine-breaking if it is a second anchor, as in `SKY-trojan-world`. **Names a real tension with the Lorenz guard-rail**: co-orbital horseshoe dynamics are chaotic on long horizons, so this can never be a forward integrator seeded from quantized ledger floats — it needs either a closed-form libration evaluated at t (the model card's evaluate-at-t rule) or a full-precision checkpoint format of its own | raw | low | [frontier §map](frontier.md#the-frontier-map) |
| SKY-quasi-satellite | A body in *stellar* orbit that nonetheless **appears to circle the world**, for millennia, without ever being gravitationally bound to it — real: 3753 Cruithne is Earth's. A "moon" that is not a moon: present in the sky, absent from the gravity model, raising no tide (SKY-5) and obeying no Kepler period about the anchor. Additive and cheap, being a sky-appearance draw rather than a dynamics change — and it is the sharpest *epistemic* body the domain could hold: a measuring culture that assumes everything circling it is bound derives a mass that does not exist. UNI-1's anomaly move (kin to `SKY-equation-of-time`'s lying sundial) handed a body instead of a curve. **Filed by The Reckoning** as the sibling deficit to its shipped capture draw: that campaign gave the model a body whose *origin* is alien; this one banks a body whose *bondage* is illusory | raw | med | [frontier §map](frontier.md#the-frontier-map); [The Reckoning](../chronicle/the-reckoning.md) |
| SKY-submoon | A moon of a moon — the one row here with **no observed instance**, though the dynamics are unobjectionable inside a narrow stability window (a large, distant primary moon holding a small, close submoon; the window is real but tight, which is the likeliest reason none has been found). Adds a **level to the hierarchy**: `moons.rs` draws a flat list keyed to the anchor, so a submoon needs the satellite tree to nest — the same shape change `SKY-moon-world` makes at the top of the tree, made at the bottom. The payoff is a sky where one moon visibly holds another, and phases within phases; the risk is that an honest stability window almost never yields one, making it a draw that rarely fires | raw | med | [frontier §map](frontier.md#the-frontier-map) |
| SKY-minimoon | Temporary capture — a body held for a few orbits and then lost; real and recurrent, with 2006 RH120 and 2020 CD3 each Earth's for roughly a year. **A moon with an expiry date**: the only body in the domain whose existence is a function of *when you look* — a satellite your grandchildren will not have and your grandparents did not. Additive (a drawn capture epoch and duration over the shipped moon machinery) but it breaks one quiet assumption worth naming: the moon roster is a genesis-time constant today, not a function of `WorldTime`. Kin to `SKY-guest-stars` in event-shape (the transient that happens once) but satellite-grade, and the natural companion to `SKY-moon-individuation`'s captured-origin draw — which banks capture as a *permanent* origin story, never as a thing that un-happens. **Filed by The Reckoning, whose permanent capture has now shipped**, which sharpens this row from a companion idea into a named deficit: astronomy draws `Capture` as a genesis-time outcome, so the assumption this row breaks — that the moon roster is a constant, not a function of `WorldTime` — is now load-bearing in merged code rather than merely implicit | raw | med | [frontier §map](frontier.md#the-frontier-map); [The Reckoning](../chronicle/the-reckoning.md) |
| SKY-s-type-binary | The world orbits **one** star of a binary while the companion hangs in the sky as an intensely bright non-sun — real, and the nearest system to us: the α Centauri configuration. Distinct from SKY-16, whose picture is the circumbinary/Tatooine regime (two suns, doubled shadows, a compound day, the host itself binary). Here the host stays single and the companion is a *second light source*, not a second primary: bright enough to cast a shadow and to kill true night for part of the year, never bright enough to be a sun. That makes it **additive where SKY-16 is spine-breaking** — a drawn companion mass and separation feeding brightness and a long orbital beat, with no second host and no compound day. The cheapest real entry into binarity, and the row that most changes the value of night (`SKY-diffuse-sky`, `SKY-galactic-situation`) | raw | med | [frontier §map](frontier.md#the-frontier-map) |
| SKY-moonlight-occlusion | The **third** occluder. Daylight hides the stars (the venue split) and cloud now dims them (The Occlusion); a full moon washing out the faint neighbour stars is the same mechanism a third time — and the only one astronomy could own *entirely alone*, with no weather knowledge at all, since it already holds every moon's phase and angular diameter. Feeds the shipped `Visibility` seam, so the machinery exists; what is missing is the brightness model that turns phase plus size into a sky-glow ratio. The row that makes a full-moon night feel different from a new-moon one | raw | high (small) | [The Occlusion](../chronicle/the-occlusion.md) |

## The climate domain — enrichment directions

Twenty-one enrichments of the *shipped* climate crate (`domains/climate`:
tier-1 `GeneratedClimate` derives temperature, moisture, a 22-class biome
field, and a binary habitability mask over the shared Geosphere), generated by
a 2026-07-10 ideonomy pass over its current shape. IDs are category+slug per
decision [`0026-slugs-not-numbers`](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/decisions/0026-slugs-not-numbers.md).
**Conf** reads as in the SKY atlas: *how cheap and clearly-correct the work
is*. The abstraction-lift framing that organizes them: the model is a field of
potential (insolation) redistributed by transport operators (winds, currents)
against radiative sinks and moisture sources, bent by feedback loops — and
today it has exactly one transport channel (zonal wind, used once for the rain
shadow) and **zero closed feedback loops**, every field a single analytic
pass. The three load-bearing moves: `CLIM-operators` (a relaxation/operator
spine) is the enabler the feedback rows all need; `CLIM-ocean-currents` is the
highest-fidelity single addition (the model card's headline omission); and
`CLIM-paleoclimate-coupling` is the highest-leverage for the wider sim,
turning climate from a day-0 snapshot into history's first substrate on
machinery MAP-6 already shipped.

| ID | Idea | Status | Conf | Where |
| -- | ---- | ------ | ---- | ----- |
| CLIM-operators | The enabling refactor — recast `generate()` from a one-shot monolith into named, individually-testable operators (insolation → advection → precipitation → feedback relaxation) that compose, so every feedback row below lands as a module without editing the others: the "adding a domain never edits an existing one" constitutional rule taken one level down, into the crate. Do it first, or the other twenty fight the monolith. **Re-timed (The Gyre, 2026-07-19):** its trigger is **cyclicity** (a feedback loop needing relaxation), not the number of fields — an ideonomy pass established that vector fields alone (The Gyre) earn none of it, correcting The Turning §7's plan to pull it into the winds campaign. It moves to the **level-2 feedback campaign** (`CLIM-ocean-currents` SST advection / `CLIM-ice-albedo`), where the first loop demands the solver spine. | raw | high | this conversation; re-timed by The Gyre |
| CLIM-ocean-currents | The model card's headline omission — a wind-driven surface-current field (gyres from the band winds × a Coriolis sign × coastline deflection) advecting the SST field, warming poleward-western coasts and cooling equatorward-eastern ones, moderating continentality from the sea. The single highest-fidelity addition; feeds marine biomes and coastal land temperature. **The vector field shipped (The Gyre, 2026-07-19, Weather Program C2)** — level 0: an Ekman-deflected, coast-projected kinematic current field emitted as `scene/tiles/v1` `current_east`/`current_north`, advected on the Living Globe; byte-identical (no temperature coupling). The **SST-advection feedback** (the coastal-moderation payoff — it moves the census-read mean → an epoch) is deliberately deferred to the level-2 feedback campaign, which carries `CLIM-operators`. | raw | med | [The Gyre spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-19-ocean-currents-design.md) (vector field shipped); SST feedback raw |

Surface strangeness on possession's existing `map` verb so a walker gets a gradient to follow rather than an answer handed over — a path, not a spoiler table. Scoped into The Occlusion's plan and dropped under its own escape hatch once `map` proved a substantial chart renderer with its own zoom and bounds handling, rather than the wiring job it looked like | raw | med | [The Occlusion](../chronicle/the-occlusion.md) |
| LOC-examine-head-noun | **A room names things a player cannot name back.** `examine` resolves by whole-string equality against the noun catalog, whose keys are the biome and the regime descriptor *verbatim* — so `examine tropical seasonal forest` answers while `examine forest` refuses, and `a stream gully, shaded, in a hollow` is unreachable as `stream`. The datum is present and its name is unsayable: nothing in the pipeline knows a noun phrase has a head. Wants a stated resolution policy — head nouns, aliases, and how an ambiguous prefix breaks *deterministically* — rather than more catalog entries | shipped | high | [The Handle](../chronicle/the-handle.md); [spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-the-handle-design.md) |
| LOC-sky-is-one-noun | **The sky is one opaque noun.** The focalizer registers a single `sky` entry whose datum is the whole sky report, so `examine moon` refuses in a room whose description names two, while `examine sky` echoes the passage back. `SkyReport.bodies` carries a per-body list, but `Vantage.sky` is a bare `String` and drops it — and its entries (`the sun`, `moon 1`) are not the prose's epithets (`the vast moon`), which `sky_at_visibility` composes inline. Prose names and structured names are separately derived, so astronomy must expose the epithet; parsing the prose back is the wrong direction | shipped | high | [The Handle](../chronicle/the-handle.md); [spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-the-handle-design.md) |
| LOC-biome-facets | The biome taxonomy as `realm : formation : stratum : variant : overlay` rather than one flat enum — `Savanna` and `Bathypelagic` are not siblings, and the classifier's precedence chain (returning a *community* where a *stratum* was expected) was the symptom. **Campaign 1 shipped in The Formations:** `Biome` survives as the *projection* of a `BiomeExpr`, so nine consuming crates were untouched and no world byte moved; realm is a triple, so a sky realm or a plane is a new value, not a new axis. Remaining: variants and their gloss epoch, exotic commensurability, the depth band | shipped | high | [The Stratum spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-the-stratum-design.md); [The Formations](../chronicle/the-formations.md) |

## The representability audit — a scene read for what the world cannot hold

A 2026-08-12 ideonomy session over the *A Game of Thrones* prologue, read as a
**capability probe**: not what the scene means, but which of its constituent
phenomena Hornvale can and cannot represent. Seven tuples (negation,
abstraction-lift, substitution, combination, cross-domain re-instantiation,
tree-finding, dimension-identification, organon-construction). The
[encodability cascade](frontier.md#the-encodability-cascade--why-the-unprecedented-cannot-be-reported)
read the same text for political economy a day earlier; this is its other side,
and the two meet at the cascade's fourth gate — see
[frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt),
where the three `elaborated` rows below are argued.

The instrument was the **concept manifest's three correspondence ledgers**
(lexeme / percept / cognition), whose trial balance is lopsided in a way no
domain listing reveals: over 207 concepts, lexeme covered 68, **percept
covered 10**, **cognition covered 2**. Read forward it finds *words without a
model*; read in reverse, *model without words*. Every claim below was checked
against code rather than inferred.

Siblings elsewhere in this registry, since the links run one way into them:
[[BIO-7]] (fauna on the life-history axis) and [[BIO-8]] (domestication &
agriculture) are the existing homes for the biosphere half — `BIO-animal-domestication`
sharpens BIO-8 rather than restating it. The cascade's own rows carry the
social half.

| ID | Idea | Status | Conf | Where |
| -- | ---- | ------ | ---- | ----- |
| KNOW-uncertainty-is-epistemic | In a deterministic world there is no aleatory uncertainty available: the world is a total function and an observer is a partial evaluation, so every doubt a creature holds must be incomplete observation, never a dice roll. A ranger's "a fortnight, if it snows" is a forecast from signs — a fact about the ranger — because the world already knows that cell's weather that day. Modelled as a random variable it gives the world a second, contradictory account of its own physics. Constrains every row here that touches doubt | elaborated | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| KNOW-doctrine-scale | The partial view already exists as a first-class object — the vessel's per-agent `Knowledge` store and the sensed/remembered split — at the individual game layer and nowhere else. No domain holds what a *people* believes as distinct from what is true. That is exactly where the cascade's gate 4 (model adequacy) lives, so doctrine is a culture-scale `Knowledge` object: an existing mechanism one layer down, not a missing one. Carries both mirrored gate-4 failures — an absent key, and a key whose extension is nowhere — and makes the back-edge a write and borrowing a copy | elaborated | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| PSY-expertise-per-individual | `domains/person` is a seed plus an empty marker struct: no skill, expertise or trained competence anywhere in the workspace, and per-species vectors where per-person ones would go. The consequence is sharper than a feature gap — the cascade's own anti-moral discipline requires competence and correctness be drawn **separately**, so it **cannot currently be falsified in simulation**. Makes this a precondition of that cluster rather than a sibling. The probe scene routes five non-overlapping specialisms and fails by mis-routing, not by incompetence | elaborated | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| BIO-decay-closes-the-chain | `decay` is not a new subsystem: it is the return edge that closes the land trophic chain (`PHOTOSYNTHATE` → `PLANT_FORAGE` → `ANIMAL_PREY`), which today terminates with nothing returning to soil. Shape it as a third `Substrate` implementor beside `Snowpack` and `SurfaceWetness` — source is flesh, sink is degree-day accumulation above freezing — and "cold preserves the dead" falls out of calibrated machinery instead of being asserted. Closes the individual-scale half of a loop the kernel already runs at population-flux scale | raw | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| BIO-exposure-inverts-decay | Hypothermia is decay's integrator with the sign flipped: exposure accumulated against a temperature deficit on a living body, versus decay against a surplus on a dead one. Both are source/sink reservoirs, and the probe text supplies a nine-point scale with named intermediates. One honest constraint on unifying them: `Substrate` steps in days while hypothermia resolves sub-day, so the seam falls on the domain/window boundary — decay day-stepped in a domain, exposure tick-stepped where the vessel's clock lives | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| BIO-life-death-corpse | The registry holds the act `die` and the residue `bone` — the far end of the somatic cycle — and skips the middle: no `life`, no `death`, no `corpse`. The gap is systematic, not local: every registered act (`eat`, `drink`, `move`, `rest`, `sleep`) lacks a corresponding state, so the vocabulary has verbs and no nominalizations. A corpse is the load-bearing one, because retaining posture and wounds is what makes a body readable as evidence | raw | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| BIO-body-rung | The scale ladder is strong from planetary down to room and absent at the **body**, and this gap is the inverse of the usual one: the vocabulary is already registered (`eye`, `hand`, `foot`, `mouth`, `bone`, `blood`, lexemes covered) with no model assembling it, while `allometry` is body-as-scaling-law. Injuries in the probe scene are *located* — ears, toes, a finger, a wound beneath an arm, a shard through one pupil — and there is no locus to put them at | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| BIO-animal-domestication | Sharpens [[BIO-8]]: the registry already admits domestication for the **plant** kingdom (barley, wheat, rice, millet, tuber, with a crops model behind them) and refuses it for the animal kingdom — every one of the ~30 registered `*-kind` fauna is wild. A working animal is therefore the missing half of an existing axis, not a new category, and it is the only creature whose distribution culture sets rather than niche, which nothing in demography models. Varieties are a breeding-for-use layer over one kind — the same layer wheat needs | raw | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| PERC-venue-audible | `Venue` is day-sky, night-sky, ambient, and `PerceptionLens` weights exactly those three: nothing in the world is ever *heard*. Audition is the probe scene's second channel throughout — a wolf, a snow owl, a stream, an instruction to listen to the darkness, a keening where metal should have rung. The enum is additive and cheap; the hard half is separable and is `PERC-absence-percept` | raw | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| PERC-absence-percept | Salience is currently a property of a thing that is present, yet the probe scene's highest-salience observations are all negative — no fire burning, no one moving, no sound, and above all a camp whose bodies are gone. An absence is only perceptible against an expectation, so this is parasitic on memory rather than on the senses, and rides the same sensed/remembered split the possession chart already carries. Cheap once memory is the baseline; impossible without it | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| PERC-being-watched | A phenomenon whose referent is the observer: the sense of being watched by something cold that loves you not. Not a venue, and it lands one gate upstream of the cascade — in the probe scene it is correct, unencodable, and the first true fact in the story. Wants a home that is neither a sky nor an ambient field | raw | low | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| PERC-senses-beyond-vision | The observation stack is a **vision** stack: a rich spectral `Observer` (N channels, per-channel roles, declared projections) and a `PerceptionVector` of activity, night-vision and sky-attention — three axes, all visual or temporal. Hearing, touch, taste and pain are absent. Smell appears nowhere in the probe text at all, which is a property of its human literate narrator, and smell is exactly the sense a tracking species would need. Possession answers "whose eyes" with no counterpart for "whose nose" | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| PERC-affordance-line | The concept manifest audits four reverse directions and declares the fifth — player-facing prose vocabulary — unaudited, pending a design line between a nameable thing and mere texture. Candidate criterion: **actionable earns a concept, decorative is texture.** Two things already sit on the wrong side of it: a fully implemented vantage that no concept names, and a fire's reach. Would convert the one unaudited direction into a fifth check | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| PERC-fire-output-vector | A fire is a multi-output emitter — warmth, light to see by, visibility at distance, predator deterrence, smoke, signal — of which two are modelled. The third needs no mechanism at all: shadowcast is symmetric between passable cells, and a shipped test asserts that light reaches exactly what sight reaches, so "a fire is the last thing we want" is already a **theorem** of the engine rather than a rule to author. Naming the affordance is the whole of the work; deterrence waits on fauna | raw | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| MAT-object-genus | There is no concept for *object*, and the shortfall is a missing **branch** rather than a missing leaf: sword → weapon → tool → artifact → object has no member registered anywhere, and the artifact branch's sole inhabitant is `hearth`. The registry is a natural-history vocabulary — biomes, star classes, ocean layers, landforms, wild fauna, weather, colour, kin — with a thin social overlay and no material culture. Nothing else material can be added cleanly until the genus exists | raw | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| MAT-use-value | Artifacts need a use-value-and-purpose facet from the start, because purpose is what converts an object's presence or absence into evidence. The probe scene's clue is a valuable axe left untouched beside a hand: the inference is *nobody abandons a thing this useful*, so the scene is wrong. Identity alone cannot support that reasoning | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| MAT-worn-affiliation | Membership is a **garment** — joining the order in the probe text is "putting on the black", one character is drawn entirely through his wardrobe, and his opponent answers by baring what frostbite took. Clothing is the cheapest physical carrier of rank, membership, wealth and competence-claims, which sharpens `MAT-object-genus`. Cross-domain gives **sumptuary law**, and whether a people regulates dress is derivable from the status basis the composition root already reads for selection temperature — an institution falling out of an existing vector rather than authored | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| SOC-gender-and-age-grade | The concept registry holds kinship (`person`, `child`, `parent`, `sibling`) and **no gender axis and no age grade**; demography holds neither either, being biomass, density and trophic response. The probe text is relentlessly age-graded, and the line the whole scene is built to deliver — seeing, of a corpse, how young he was — is an age-grade reclassification that cannot be expressed. Gender does epistemic work there twice, as an authority discount and as a courage predicate, which is the cascade's gate 3 under a different sorting key | raw | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| SOC-abort-precommitment | A refinement to the cascade's counterweight. Its stated remedy is a compulsory upward-sampling rite; aviation's two-challenge rule and phase-bound callouts, mountaineering's turnaround time, and the read-aloud surgical checklist all converge on something narrower — **phase-bound, scripted, and fixed before the gradient exists**. Precommitment is strongest because the subordinate need not speak at all, and its own failure mode, ossification, keeps it a mechanism rather than a moral. The probe scene's first line of speech is a refused turnaround call | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| SOC-watch-rota | A garrison's watch rotation is a periodic institutional schedule, and the liveness layer already derives deterministic daily routes for NPCs — so institutional periodicity is a short step from shipped, and it is the cheapest thing that makes an institution observably *run* rather than merely exist | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| KNOW-thing-provenance | The object-level twin of the cascade's gate 2: that gate asks whether an *utterance* carries where it came from, this asks whether a **thing** does. The probe scene's dominant abstract noun is proof, and every object in it is weighed as evidence — a broken sword kept as testimony, a cold firepit, a body's posture. The ledger has a contradiction check and no notion of evidence or of a trace's reliability. Design the two halves together | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| KNOW-spoor-is-stratigraphy | Tracks are stratigraphy at the resolution of an afternoon. The lifted shape — the world writes a decaying record of its own past onto itself, and a competent observer reads it backwards — already has four implementations (ice cores, lithology, historiography's fact replay, the ledger readback), at ten-thousand-year and geologic resolution and never at a timescale a person walks across. The eraser is already modelled too: fresh snowfall is what covers a camp | raw | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| KNOW-intentionality-grade | Trail-reading needs an intentionality grade on a residue, not just the residue: accidental emission (tracks, posture, blood, breath) versus designed residue (a lean-to, a firepit) versus contested. The probe scene stages the dispute directly — bodies read as *fallen*, answered with *or sleeping* — and that argument is the professional core of a tracker's competence | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| KNOW-degraded-forecast | Forcing a journey into a passage-plan notation leaves five slots empty and all five are about doubt: a degraded arrival estimate, weather minima, reserve, alternates, and a point of no return. "Snow is the best we can hope for" names a distribution's good tail, not a forecast. Must be built as knowledge, never as a roll — see `KNOW-uncertainty-is-epistemic` | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| KNOW-proxy-inference | A gap the cascade's four gates do not cover, found twice in the probe scene: a percept licensing the **refutation of a causal hypothesis**. Meltwater on a wall is read as a thermometer, and the conclusion is that the cold cannot have killed these men. That is neither gate 1 (can it be said) nor gate 3 (is it weighted by standing) — it is reasoning from an observation to a claim about a *different* thing, and with cognition covered at 2 of 207 concepts there is nothing to do it with. The scene's one moment where rank and correctness agree | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| LANG-numeracy-gate | The registry's numerals are `one`, `two`, `many`, and a one-two-many tongue **cannot say "eight"** — the cascade's first gate arriving at arithmetic, with a numeracy module already present to decide which tongues are so limited. The probe scene's counts are also estimates carrying error rather than ledger entries: a band counted three, then four, then five, and a camp census hedged as no children *that I could see* | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| LANG-dyadic-register | The register renderer is a real content-to-render seam with per-species voice knobs, but register is **per-species, not per-dyad**. The natural extension of a seam that already exists rather than a new subsystem | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |

Rungs: number on both sides; a transitive frame; per-tongue role surfaces; tense (drawn, nothing to inflect); recognition, which `sentences/` measures before growing. Coverage 0/12, honestly | elaborated | high | [The Interlinear](../chronicle/the-interlinear.md) |
| MAP-small-group-roster | A hole in the middle of the scale ladder: 2–20 individuals, each individuated, too few to be a density and too many to be the one possessed agent. A **roster** is the right structure, and it is neither a rate nor a singleton — the probe scene lives entirely in this band, reporting eight in a camp, men and women both. The liveness layer's derived NPCs are its near edge | raw | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| MAP-intraday-order | The day is the one resolution at which nothing in the probe scene happens: its drama runs in seconds to minutes and its institutions in decades to generations. Since a fact is stamped with a day, a duel's *sequence* is expressible only as append order, not as time order. The ladder exists on both sides — ticks below in the vessel's clock, years above in the chronicle — so this is a thing to know before trying to commit a fight, not necessarily a thing to fix | raw | low | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| MAP-climb-affordance | `climb` is not a sibling of `move`: moving needs only a bearing, climbing needs a **structure with purchase**. Adding the act beside the other acts would miss the part that makes it work | raw | med | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| PERC-concept-valence | **Rejected: no valence column on the concept manifest.** Cold is strongly negative to a man who lost two ears, three toes and a finger to it, and he narrates its ending as seduction; fire is safety to him and betrayal to his commander, in the same minute, about the same fire. One kind per animal, with varieties as a breeding-for-use layer; see `BIO-animal-domestication` | rejected | high | [frontier §partial-view](frontier.md#the-partial-view--where-a-deterministic-world-keeps-its-doubt) |
| BIO-gause-distinctness-vacuous | **The cv-ratio instrument can no longer tell human from goblin, and all three of its arms collapsed together.** Real 0.9945, goblin-niche-substituted 0.9964, width-only 0.9964 (was 0.9747), so the real gap 0.0055 misses the 0.007 floor and the residual real-vs-mutated difference is 0.0019. Neither niche changed; The Glasshouse's climate correction moved the fit landscape under both. The readout is vacuous until a statistic with power against this world replaces it. | raw | high (measured) | `windows/worldgen/tests/generalist_distinctness.rs` (witness: `the_collapsed_cv_ratio_arms_are_pinned_as_witnesses`) |
| BIO-raid-partition-order-statistic | **The raider floor is measuring a post-epoch world at a pre-epoch scale.** Distinct from `TOOL-min-vs-max-separation-compares-an-overlap`, which decision 0134 retired while KEEPING this floor: it held at 0.433 when 0134 was written, then The Glasshouse's climate correction put drow at 14/60 = 0.233 under the 0.30 bar and The Underworld took it to 12/60 = 0.200 — numerator only, denominator 60 both times. The stated mechanism, a raid branch that stopped running, is refuted by 12 live re-seats where sea-elf at 0/60 shows a dead branch. Needs a re-fit against post-epoch rates, not a lowered bar. | raw | high (measured) | `windows/lab/tests/disposition_calibration.rs::every_raider_clears_the_floor_preregistered_not_met` (witness: `the_sub_floor_raider_reading_is_pinned_as_a_witness`) |
| TOOL-session-cost-has-no-canonical-basis | **`session_cost`'s millisecond ceilings were calibrated on aarch64-10 and the heavy tier now runs on x86_64-40.** The test already declines to compute its ratio and verdict off `BASIS_HOST`, then asserted absolute ms ceilings anyway: measured 2026-08-15, one turn read 14.710 ms against an 8 ms ceiling on lefford under the heavy tier's own load, while the same commit passed on a quiet Mac. The assertions are now scoped to the basis host; the durable fix is a calibrated x86_64-40 basis set. | raw | med | `cli/tests/session_cost.rs` (the `bases_apply` guard) |

The wider infrastructure layer this row names (named rivers as entities, trade routes, borders, crossings/fords, bridges) is still unbuilt | shipped (settlement-siting slice) | high | [frontier §year-1 sequencing](frontier.md#two-sequencing-notes-for-the-remaining-year-1-campaigns); [The Freshet chronicle](../chronicle/the-freshet.md); [The Confluence chronicle](../chronicle/the-confluence.md) |

| SEQ-5 | The observer has no place — phenomena are delivered position-blind. `ObserverContext.place` is an `EntityId` with no location on the globe, so the sky can't be culled by horizon: on a tidally-locked world the fixed sun reaches its own night side and the neighbour stars reach the permanent day side, and on a spinning world the moons/stars gate on the *global* `is_daylight` clock, not the observer's longitude. The spatial sibling of SEQ-4 and of EXP-3's *perceptual* observer — the fix extends `ObserverContext` (not `Phenomenon`; position is the observer's, not the body's), the seam MAP-2's "one hemisphere of sky" almanac assumes | shipped        | high | [Firm Ground II spec](https://github.com/hornvale/hornvale/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-firm-ground-ii-design.md)   |
